This paper introduces Spectral Clustering with Feature Selection (SC-FS), a novel approach that first generates initial labels using spectral clustering, then identifies a subset of features exhibiting the highest R-squared values relative to these labels, and finally performs clustering on the selected features. Under mild assumptions, we demonstrate that SC-FS successfully recovers all informative features with high probability and attains the minimax optimal clustering error rate within the sparse Gaussian mixture model framework. Furthermore, applications to four real-world datasets illustrate the method's effectiveness in clustering high-dimensional data.

This paper examines a partial sorting algorithm applied to permutations in one-line notation, which involves moving the first element to the position corresponding to its value until the sequence begins with 1. This operation defines a forest structure on permutations of size $n$, with roots being those starting with 1 and leaves representing derangements. Reversing this process, one selects a fixed point and relocates it to the front. Although simple, this "fixed point forest" displays complex properties. By analyzing the limit as $n \to \infty$ using Stein's method, we demonstrate that the local structure at a random permutation weakly converges to a tree constructed from independent Poisson point processes. Furthermore, the distribution of the longest path to a leaf approaches a geometric distribution with mean $e-1$, while the shortest path distribution converges to a Poisson distribution with mean 1. Additionally, the boundedness of higher moments ensures that expectations converge.

New solutions to the elliptic Darboux equation are derived as specific instances of solutions to Heun's general equation. This work examines two sets of power series expansions alongside two novel groups of series based on Gauss hypergeometric functions. The convergence of one power series group is established using ratio tests for infinite series, whereas the other groups are tailored for problems allowing finite-series solutions. Specifically, these methods address periodic quasi-exactly solvable potentials, reducing the stationary one-dimensional Schrödinger equation to the Darboux equation. While finite- and infinite-series solutions are typically generated from power series expansions of Heun's equation, we demonstrate that the Schrödinger equation supports additional finite-series expansions in terms of hypergeometric functions for a specific family of associated Lamé potentials relevant to the band theory of solids. For every finite-series solution identified, we also derive four bounded, convergent infinite-series expansions valid for all values of the independent variable. Finally, we establish that variable transformations can be employed to generate new Darboux equation solutions from other hypergeometric series expansions of the Heun equation.

The widespread presence of sequences across various fields has fueled recent interest in sequence learning, with a fundamental challenge being the measurement of distance between them. Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) addresses this by aligning sequences through nonlinear local warping to produce a distance metric, demonstrating superior performance in applications such as video and image analysis. However, DTW pairs points primarily based on Euclidean distance (ED) without accounting for sequence autocorrelation. Consequently, points with distinct semantic roles, such as peaks and valleys, may be incorrectly matched if their coordinate values are similar, rendering DTW sensitive to noise and difficult to interpret. To address these limitations, this paper introduces Dynamic State Warping (DSW), an efficient and flexible alignment algorithm. DSW transforms each time point into a latent state, thereby incorporating point-wise autocorrelation information; alignment is then executed using these state sequences, resulting in outcomes that are more semantically interpretable than those of DTW. Furthermore, when evaluated with a one-nearest-neighbor classifier, DSW achieves significantly higher classification accuracy compared to both ED (70/85 wins) and DTW (74/85 wins). Empirical results also confirm that DSW offers greater robustness and scales more effectively for long sequences than its ED and DTW counterparts.

We establish an explicit criterion based on the Walsh spectrum that determines when $p$-ary functions generate association schemes. Utilizing this characterization, we explicitly identify a relationship between $p$-ary bent functions and association schemes; specifically, we demonstrate that a $p$-ary bent function yields a $p$-class association scheme if and only if it is weakly regular. As applications of our primary criterion, we construct numerous infinite families of few-class association schemes derived from $p$-ary functions. Additionally, we introduce four classes of $p$-ary two-weight linear codes, which are built upon the association schemes generated in this study.

This study introduces a distributed framework utilizing distinct estimators to achieve event-triggered formation control for polytopic homogeneously scheduled linear parameter-varying (LPV) multi-agent systems (MAS). Each agent features a time-triggered inner feedback loop paired with a larger event-triggered outer loop, designed to track formation references while mitigating input and output noise. When a local event-trigger condition is breached, the outer feedback loop engages via the communication network, relying solely on locally accessible data for the trigger condition. The controller design is formulated as a linear matrix inequality of single-agent size, assuming that local estimators initiate inter-agent communication upon condition violation. This approach ensures stability and bounded $l_2$-performance, with the added flexibility that estimators can be swapped for a specific controller. Simulations compare zero-order hold, open-loop, and closed-loop estimation strategies using non-holonomic dynamic unicycles modeled as polytopic LPV systems.

Directional modulation (DM) serves as a highly effective secure transmission technique, leveraging its directive capabilities for line-of-sight (LoS) channels such as millimeter-wave massive MIMO, satellite links, UAV communications, and smart transportation systems. When the direction angle of the intended receiver is known, the corresponding channel gain vector becomes determinable. Consequently, the DM transmitter can pre-calculate the directional angles of both the legitimate user and potential eavesdroppers, as the beamforming vector for confidential messages and the projection matrix for artificial noise are primarily dictated by these angles. For a DM transceiver operating in reception mode, the process begins by measuring the directions of arrival (DOAs) of the desired user and eavesdropper. Subsequently, these measured DOAs are utilized to design the beamforming vector for confidential data and the artificial noise projection matrix. This paper outlines DOA measurement techniques, power allocation strategies, and beamforming methods within DM networks. Specifically, we propose a machine learning-based DOA measurement approach that achieves significant signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) performance gains compared to single-snapshot measurements without machine learning, particularly when using null-space projection beamforming. However, conventional DM networks face a critical security vulnerability: if an eavesdropper moves into the main lobe of the desired user's beam, they may intercept confidential messages, as the current beamforming and noise projection vectors rely solely on angular dependence. To mitigate this, we introduce a novel concept of secure and precise transmission. This approach ensures two-dimensional or three-dimensional waveform dependence at the DM transmitter by integrating DM, random frequency selection, and phase alignment.

This paper examines the uniqueness of solutions for differential and algebraic operator Riccati equations, subject to specific conditions regarding their unbounded coefficients. The boundary control systems defined by these assumptions include various significant physical interactions, which are modeled using coupled systems of hyperbolic and parabolic partial differential equations. The uniqueness proofs presented address and resolve challenges stemming from the unique regularity characteristics of the composite dynamics. Furthermore, these findings extend the linear-quadratic theories for both finite and infinite time horizons developed jointly by the authors and Lasiecka, as the unique Riccati solution is integral to the closed-loop structure of optimal control.

This research investigates the hydrodynamic limit of a symmetric exclusion process featuring heavy-tailed long jumps and interaction with infinitely extended reservoirs. We demonstrate how the model's defining parameters influence the resulting hydrodynamic equations. These equations are distinguished by a set of super-diffusive operators, specifically regional fractional Laplacians augmented with reaction terms and diverse boundary conditions. Furthermore, this study addresses several unresolved questions from \cite{BJGO2} regarding this particular model.

Correlated photons drive numerous metrology platforms that leverage quantum (anti-)correlations to surpass classical light sources. Although existing demonstrations primarily emphasize entanglement, the potential of photon exchange-phase and distinguishability remains underutilized in quantum-enhanced applications. Through an interferometric configuration, we demonstrate that even with low entanglement, coupling a two-photon wave-function to matter encodes reliable "which-path" information. We introduce an interferometric exchange-phase-cycling protocol that allows for phase-sensitive discrimination of microscopic interaction histories. Our results reveal that quantum-light interferometry accesses a unique set of time-delay variables, unconstrained by the uncertainty relation between time and the inverse wave-packet bandwidth. We validate these findings using an exciton model system, showing how intraband dephasing can be probed in the time domain without requiring temporal resolution at the detector. Additionally, we examine the unusual scaling of multiphoton coincidence rates relative to applied intensity.

Detecting pedestrians in dense crowds is difficult due to the frequent mutual occlusion of individuals, which creates ambiguity and complicates the IoU-based ground truth assignment used in traditional object detection. This paper introduces a novel approach by reframing pedestrian detection as a variational inference problem. We propose an efficient algorithm that models dense proposals as latent variables within a customized Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes (AEVB) framework. By optimizing this algorithm, standard detectors can be transformed into variational pedestrian detectors. Experimental results on the CrowdHuman and CityPersons datasets demonstrate that our method effectively addresses the challenges of single-stage dense pedestrian detection. Furthermore, the approach is adaptable to two-stage detectors, yielding significant performance improvements.

We examine the vacuum partition function of a 4d scalar quantum field theory in a curved background, treating it as a function of bare marginal and relevant couplings. By introducing a local UV cutoff $\Lambda(x)$ that transforms under Weyl rescalings, we construct Weyl-invariant kinetic terms that incorporate Wilsonian cutoff functions. This local cutoff can be entirely absorbed through a rescaling of the metric and the bare couplings. The vacuum partition function adheres to consistency conditions derived from the Abelian character of local cutoff redefinitions, which are distinct from Weyl rescalings. These conditions yield a gradient flow for beta functions that describes how rescaled bare couplings depend on the cutoff. Furthermore, these consistency conditions enable the satisfaction of all Hamiltonian constraints required for a holographic description of the bare coupling flow, except for one.

Neural Style Transfer (NST) has rapidly advanced from handling single styles to infinite-style Arbitrary Style Transfer (AST). Despite the impressive results widely documented in literature, our empirical evaluation of four prominent AST methods (GoogleMagenta, AdaIN, LinearTransfer, and SANet) reveals that over 50% of the generated stylized images fail to meet human standards, primarily due to under- or over-stylization. We systematically investigate the causes of this imbalanced style transferability (IST) and introduce a straightforward yet effective solution to address it. Our findings indicate that the IST problem stems from conventional AST style losses, where equal weighting of training samples regardless of their style image properties biases the model toward specific styles. By analyzing the theoretical limits of AST style loss, we propose a new loss function that significantly mitigates IST. Both theoretical analysis and experimental results confirm the efficacy of our approach, demonstrating an 80% relative increase in style deception rate and a 98% higher preference score in human evaluations.

Recent methods for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning under the \emph{centralized training with decentralized execution} paradigm typically rely on estimating a centralized, joint value function. However, this paper shows that Independent PPO (IPPO)—an independent learning approach where each agent estimates only its local value function—can match or surpass state-of-the-art joint learning methods on the SMAC benchmark suite with minimal hyperparameter adjustment. Furthermore, comparisons with various IPPO variants indicate that its superior performance likely stems from robustness against certain types of environment non-stationarity.

The Clustered Shortest-Path Tree Problem (CluSPT) represents an NP-hard challenge within literature, where prior research typically navigates a vast solution space. To improve search efficiency, two novel approaches are introduced. The first targets edge-based solutions by constructing a reduced graph with significantly fewer vertices than the original, enabling an effective Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) to solve CluSPT. The second approach focuses on vertex-based solutions by transforming the CluSPT search space into two nested layers (NSS). In this framework, the lower-level search engine identifies optimal candidates to pair with each high-level optimization result, forming the best overall solution; consequently, a Nested Local Search EA (N-LSEA) is developed to optimize within this NSS structure. Furthermore, to address the variety of similar tasks encountered during lower-level optimization by N-LSEA, a Multifactorial Evolutionary Algorithm is employed to facilitate implicit genetic transfer across these processes. Experimental results on multiple datasets confirm that the proposed algorithms achieve superior efficiency compared to previous scientific studies.

We present an analysis of exclusive diphoton photoproduction within the nearly forward kinematic regime of large invariant mass, where collinear QCD factorization is valid. Our calculations are performed at leading twist and include next-to-leading order (NLO) corrections in the strong coupling constant $\alpha_S$. We compare our predicted cross-sections with Born-level results for the experimental conditions reachable at JLab, highlighting the significant sensitivity of our findings to different generalized parton distribution (GPD) models. Although the NLO corrections are notably large and negative, they do not undermine the reaction's viability as a promising method for extracting C-dd GPDs, which remain inaccessible through spacelike or timelike deeply virtual Compton scattering amplitudes.

Building on our prior research, we have devised an algorithm to calculate a presentation for the fundamental group of specific partial compactifications of the complement of a complex line arrangement in the projective plane. This method is particularly applicable to homology planes derived from line arrangements. Consequently, it allows us to establish the infinitude of the fundamental group for homology planes of log-general type, potentially providing the first examples of this category.

Current research on commonsense reasoning has primarily focused on English. Our objective is to assess and enhance popular multilingual language models (ML-LMs) to extend commonsense reasoning capabilities beyond English. We have gathered the Mickey Corpus, comprising 561k sentences across 11 languages, to facilitate the analysis and improvement of ML-LMs. Furthermore, we introduce Mickey Probe, a language-agnostic probing task designed for the fair evaluation of commonsense understanding in ML-LMs across various languages. Additionally, we developed two new datasets, X-CSQA and X-CODAH, by translating their English counterparts into 15 other languages to enable cross-lingual commonsense reasoning evaluation. To boost performance beyond English, we propose a simple yet effective technique called multilingual contrastive pre-training (MCP). This method significantly improves sentence representations, resulting in substantial performance gains on both benchmarks.

Topology has been a pivotal area of physics research over the past few decades, with particular focus on the quantum geometric tensor, which offers local insights into topological characteristics. This tensor holds the potential to uncover intriguing properties of non-Abelian systems that have yet to be practically realized. In this work, we implement a four-qubit system within superconducting circuits to engineer a degenerate Hamiltonian subject to parametric modulation. Through periodic driving of this Hamiltonian, we simulate the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang model and derive the quantum geometric tensor by analyzing interference oscillations. Furthermore, we identify its topological nature by calculating the topological invariant, thereby establishing an effective protocol for simulating non-Abelian systems.

This paper presents a formula for calculating the number of lattice points within dilated Schubert matroid polytopes. As applications, we derive the Ehrhart polynomials for uniform and minimal matroids as specific instances and provide a recursive formula for those of $(a,b)$-Catalan matroids. While Ferroni previously demonstrated the Ehrhart positivity of uniform and minimal matroids, we extend this result to show that all sparse paving Schubert matroids are also Ehrhart positive, with their polynomials coefficient-wise bounded by those of minimal and uniform matroids, thereby confirming Ferroni's conjecture for this class. Additionally, we introduce notched rectangle matroids, a broader category encompassing minimal matroids, sparse paving Schubert matroids, and panhandle matroids. We prove that three specific subfamilies of these notched rectangle matroids exhibit Ehrhart positivity and conjecture that the property holds for all such matroids.

To establish updated absolute parameters for specific close binary systems, new BVR CCD photometry was conducted at the Ankara University Observatory (AUG) between April 2007 and October 2008, focusing on five eclipsing binaries: ET Boo, V1123 Tau, V1191 Cyg, V1073 Cyg, and V357 Peg. This study presents orbital solutions derived from simultaneous analyses of light and radial velocity curves for these systems. Notably, this research provides the first-ever extensive orbital solutions and absolute parameters for the ET Boo system. The analyses reveal that ET Boo is a detached binary, whereas the remaining four systems exhibit characteristics consistent with contact binaries. Furthermore, the evolutionary status of the components in these systems is discussed based on the absolute parameters determined in this work.

Governments and international bodies globally are funding initiatives aimed at achieving universal energy access to foster socio-economic progress. Yet, in developing regions, tracking electrification efforts often suffers from being costly, infrequent, and imprecise. This study introduces methods for high-resolution, large-scale monitoring of electrification advancement. Our three distinct contributions are: (i) pinpointing areas with or without electricity access, (ii) measuring the degree of electrification within connected areas (by percentage or count of structures), and (iii) distinguishing between customer types in electrified zones (by estimating the proportion of residential versus non-residential structures). We integrate 50 cm daytime satellite imagery with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to train various classification and regression models. These models were validated against unique ground truth data regarding building locations, types (residential/non-residential), and electrification status. Our classification models achieved 92% accuracy in identifying electrified regions, 85% accuracy in estimating the percentage of low- or high-electrified buildings within those regions, and 69% accuracy in differentiating between low- and high-proportions of electrified residential buildings. Regression analyses yielded $R^2$ scores of 78% and 80% for estimating the total number of electrified buildings and the number of electrified residential buildings, respectively. Furthermore, we demonstrated the models' generalizability to previously unseen regions, highlighting their potential for consistent, high-resolution electrification measurement in emerging economies, and concluded by outlining areas for future improvement.

The combined density functional theory and multireference configuration interaction (DFT/MRCI) approach serves as a potent method for computing excited electronic states in large molecules. However, typical DFT/MRCI wave functions contain a significant number of redundant configurations. We demonstrate that this unnecessary "deadwood" can be efficiently eliminated through a straightforward configuration pruning algorithm grounded in second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory. The proposed technique, labeled p-DFT/MRCI, achieves computational time reductions by orders of magnitude while maintaining the accuracy of the original DFT/MRCI framework.

The notion of an intelligent system has arisen within information technology as a system type stemming from successful artificial intelligence applications. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of intelligent systems, synthesizing prior methodologies with recent AI advancements. It outlines these systems generically by defining their core properties, functional components, and common categories. Adopting a practical framework for system engineers, the description is supported by real-world examples and connected to specific AI methods.

This study examines the factors determining the initial rate of emergence of a quantum channel during the interaction of two systems, $A$ and $B$. Specifically, when system $A$ is pre-entangled with an ancilla, $\tilde{A}$, we measure the early-stage transmission of existing entanglement by computing the leading-order variation in the coherent information of the complementary channel ($A\rightarrow B'$). Our findings indicate that if $A$ and $B$ start unentangled and $B$ is pure, the coherent information remains unchanged to first order, whereas the leading second-order change diverges. This divergence can be controlled by generalizing coherent information into a family of $n$-coherent informations based on $n$-Rényi entropies. We demonstrate that the initial rate of change of $n$-coherent information is dictated by a metric termed "$n$-exposure," which reflects how much the initial entanglement between $A$ and $\tilde{A}$ is accessible to the interaction Hamiltonian between $A$ and $B$. We illustrate these concepts with examples involving qubit systems and light-matter interactions.

The Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) plans to conduct Deep Drilling Fields (DDFs) with increased depth and faster cadence compared to the main survey. This paper details the ``DeepDrill'' project, which utilized the Spitzer Space Telescope's Infrared Array Camera (IRAC) to image three of the four designated DDFs in the 3.6 $\mu$m and 4.5 $\mu$m bands. These new observations extend the coverage of the earlier Spitzer Extragalactic Representative Volume Survey (SERVS) within the same regions. Together, the DeepDrill and SERVS datasets map the LSST DDF footprints in the Extended Chandra Deep Field-South (ECDFS), ELAIS-S1 (ES1), and XMM Large-Scale Structure Survey (XMM-LSS) fields. Achieving an approximate $5\sigma$ point-source sensitivity of 2 $\mu$Jy (AB magnitude 23.1) across a combined area of roughly 29 $\text{deg}^2$, the survey is sensitive enough to detect galaxies with masses around $10^{11} M_{\odot}$ out to redshifts of $z\approx 5$. The resulting dual-band catalogues comprise 2.35 million sources. This study outlines the survey observations and data products, provides an overview of the detected galaxy population, and compares source counts against the SHARK semi-analytic galaxy formation model. Additionally, we identify a population of sources with extremely red colours ([3.6]$-$[4.5] $>1.2$), demonstrating that they are primarily highly-obscured active galactic nuclei.

Beam transfer, including injection and extraction in accelerators, represents a critical phase for machine protection in high-intensity systems. Consequently, dedicated equipment must be employed, and safety considerations are integral to designing beam transfer concepts. This lecture will provide a concise overview of the underlying principles and associated equipment for beam transfer. Furthermore, it will outline the primary machine protection strategies for both injection and extraction, illustrated with case studies from the CERN SPS and LHC.

We examine quantum mechanics on noncommutative spaces defined by the commutation relations $$ [x_a, x_b] \ =\ i\theta f_{abc} x_c\,, $$ where $f_{abc}$ denote the structure constants of a Lie algebra. This scenario can be recast as a standard quantum problem within a commuting momentum space, where coordinates are expressed as linear differential operators: $\hat x_a = -i\hat D_a = -iE_{ab} (p)\, \partial /\partial p_b$. Typically, the matrix $E_{ab}(p)$ corresponds to an infinite series in the deformation parameter $\theta$, starting with $E_{ab} = \delta_{ab} + \ldots$. The resulting deformed Hamiltonian, $\hat H = -\frac 12 \hat D_a^2\,,$ governs motion along group manifolds with a characteristic scale of order $\theta^{-1}$. The associated metrics are likewise expanded as infinite series in $\theta$, interpreting $E_{ab}$ as vielbeins. For the specific cases of $su(2)$ and $u(N)$ algebras, the operators $\hat x_a$ admit simple finite representations. Furthermore, our investigation yields novel nonstandard expressions for metrics on spheres $S^n$, projective spaces $RP^n$, and the manifold $U(2)$.

In this high-$x$ domain, the flavor composition and structural details of nucleon parton distribution functions remain largely uncertain. Recent LHCb data on associated production of Z bosons and charm jets may reveal a valence-like intrinsic charm component within the proton wave function, while Z production measurements in pPb collisions offer fresh constraints on the partonic makeup of nucleons within nuclei. This discussion focuses on these new LHCb results alongside comparisons with current state-of-the-art parton distribution function models.

Supercomputer Fugaku, currently ranked number one on the TOP500 list, has proven that CPU-only high-performance computing (HPC) systems are far from obsolete and that CPUs can perform tasks beyond merely acting as host controllers for discrete accelerators. Although chip specifications, system architecture, and benchmarks from lists like TOP500 and Green500 clearly indicate significant potential, the recent integration of Arm into the HPC sector means the software stack is not yet fully mature or optimized. To address this, we evaluated three state-of-the-art compiler suites against a wide range of benchmarks. Our results demonstrate that substantial performance gains—measured in orders of magnitude—can be achieved by departing from the standard recommended usage model for A64FX compute nodes.

Backdoor attacks typically embed fixed artifacts into deep learning models to induce targeted misclassification during testing, making them relatively easy to identify. Recently, however, researchers have introduced stylistic triggers—such as specific writing styles—that apply transformations to input samples and are significantly harder to detect. Current literature on stylistic backdoors lacks a formal framework, which this paper establishes. Furthermore, while existing studies focus on text and images, the efficacy of such triggers in audio remains unexplored. This work addresses that gap by proposing JingleBack, the first stylistic backdoor attack utilizing audio transformations like chorus and gain. Experimental results on 444 models within a speech classification task demonstrate the feasibility of these audio-based triggers, achieving a 96% attack success rate.

This paper introduces a continuation method that converts spatially distributed ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems into continuous partial differential equations (PDEs). We demonstrate that this transformation applies to both linear and nonlinear systems, encompassing multidimensional, space- and time-varying dynamics. When applied to large-scale networks, the method yields a PDE describing the evolution of a continuous state approximation that maintains the spatial structure of the original ODEs. Our approach is validated through various examples, including transport, Kuramoto, and heat diffusion equations. As a primary case study, we apply the continuation to a Newtonian system of interacting particles to derive the Euler equations for compressible fluids, offering a novel solution to Hilbert's 6th problem. Furthermore, we utilize this derivation of the Euler equations to control multi-agent systems by designing a nonlinear control algorithm for robot formation based on their continuous approximation.

This study presents a unit averaging method designed to efficiently retrieve unit-specific parameters within a heterogeneous panel model. The approach involves calculating the parameter for a specific unit as a weighted average of all unit-specific parameter estimators across the panel, where the weights are optimized by minimizing a mean squared error (MSE) criterion. We examine the properties of this minimum MSE unit averaging estimator within a local heterogeneity framework, drawing inspiration from frequentist model averaging literature. Our analysis addresses scenarios where the panel's cross-sectional dimension is either fixed or large. For both cases, we derive the local asymptotic distributions of the minimum MSE unit averaging estimators and their corresponding weights. Finally, an application of this procedure to GDP nowcasting for a panel of European countries demonstrates its advantages.

This study investigates the quantum entanglement between two coupled harmonic oscillators interacting through a magnetic coupling $\omega_{c}$ generated by angular momentum. By applying three canonical transformations, the system's Hamiltonian is diagonalized to derive the stationary wave function. Utilizing the Schmidt decomposition, we explicitly calculate the Schmidt modes $\lambda_{k}$ for $k \in \{0, 1, \dots, n+m\}$, where $n$ and $m$ represent the quantum numbers of the respective oscillators. Our analysis examines how entanglement is influenced by anisotropy ($R = \omega_{1}^{2}/\omega_{2}^{2}$), the magnetic coupling $\omega_{c}$, asymmetry ($|n-m|$), and dynamical effects, leading to the following conclusions: (i) Entanglement increases significantly as $(n, m)$ grow; (ii) The sensitivity to $\omega_{c}$ varies depending on $(n, m)$ and $R$; and (iii) The periodic revival of entanglement is heavily dependent on both physical parameters and quantum numbers.

The multigrid algorithm serves as an efficient numerical technique for addressing various elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs). By dampening errors across progressively finer grid scales, it achieves faster convergence than conventional iterative approaches like Gauss-Seidel. The algorithm's prolongation operator, which handles coarse-to-fine interpolation, is well-suited for a data-driven approach using machine learning super-resolution, a method typically employed to enhance image resolution. This work (i) introduces the innovative combination of a super-resolution generative adversarial network (GAN) as the prolongation operator within the multigrid framework, and (ii) demonstrates that this GAN-based interpolation yields superior convergence properties compared to cubic spline interpolation for a specific class of multiscale PDEs frequently encountered in physics and engineering simulations.

Typically, achieving high-performance text detection using deep networks requires extensive pre-training and prolonged training. This paper introduces FANet, a novel scene text detection network characterized by rapid convergence and precise text localization. As an end-to-end detector, FANet leverages transformer-based feature learning and normalized Fourier descriptor modeling. It employs a Fourier Descriptor Proposal Network and an Iterative Text Decoding Network to efficiently and accurately identify text proposals. Furthermore, the model incorporates a Dense Matching Strategy and a tailored loss function to optimize performance. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that FANet achieves state-of-the-art results with fewer training epochs and without any pre-training. When additional pre-training data is introduced, FANet attains SOTA performance on the MSRATD500, CTW1500, and TotalText datasets. Ablation studies further validate the efficacy of the proposed contributions.

This study introduces an analytical predictive model for interface charge traps in symmetric long-channel double-gate junctionless transistors, grounded in a charge-based framework. These traps, which can emerge from chemical exposure, high-energy ionizing radiation, or aging processes, are known to degrade charge-voltage performance. The proposed model effectively predicts behavior across a temperature spectrum ranging from 77K to 400K. Its accuracy is substantiated by comprehensive comparisons with numerical TCAD simulations, validating the approach across all operational regions, including deep depletion, accumulation, linear, and saturation modes.

This study demonstrates that an N-person non-cooperative semi-Markov game with a limiting ratio average payoff criterion possesses a pure semi-stationary Nash equilibrium. While a zero-sum two-player version was previously addressed, our proof strategy involves transforming these perfect information games into associated semi-Markov decision processes (SMDPs), leveraging existing SMDP existence theorems. This reduction technique yields straightforward proofs for several key results: (a) zero-sum two-player perfect information stochastic (Markov) games admit a value and pure stationary optimal strategies for both players under both discounted and undiscounted payoff frameworks; and (b) analogous conclusions apply to N-person non-cooperative perfect information stochastic games. Consequently, any such game can be resolved using efficient algorithms designed for the corresponding reduced SMDP (or MDP in the case of stochastic games). In this work, we apply Mondal's algorithm to solve an SMDP specifically under the limiting ratio average payoff criterion.

This research examines the connection between transitivity and topological chaos in homeomorphisms of the two-torus. We demonstrate that for a transitive homeomorphism of $\mathbb{T}^2$ homotopic to the identity, the existence of both a fixed point and a non-fixed periodic point implies the presence of a topological horseshoe. Additionally, we prove that if a transitive homeomorphism of $\mathbb{T}^2$ is homotopic to a Dehn twist, it must either be aperiodic or possess a topological horseshoe.

This article introduces a floating robotic emulation platform designed to virtually demonstrate satellite motion in space. The platform features frictionless, levitating movement within a planar configuration over a hyper-smooth surface. Developed and manufactured by the Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Team at Luleå University of Technology, the system integrates various sensor and actuator units. The paper provides a comprehensive design description and mathematical modeling of the platform's dynamic behavior. Extensive simulation studies validate the proposed design, while the experimental testbed setup, along with the vehicle's hardware and software architectures, are discussed in detail. Additionally, the complete design, including 3D printing CAD models and testbed components, is made available in an open-source repository. A test campaign is conducted to demonstrate the platform's capabilities and operational functions.

Over the next few years, demand for satellite broadband services is projected to surge, particularly within the mobility sector, which is characterized by highly variable traffic patterns. As the next generation of satellites incorporates extensive flexibility in power and bandwidth distribution, manual resource management will become both inefficient and unfeasible, necessitating automated operational systems. This study introduces a new power allocation strategy utilizing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), which models the problem within continuous state and action spaces. By employing the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm, we optimize the allocation policy to minimize both Unmet System Demand (USD) and power consumption. Simulations of a multibeam satellite system demonstrate the algorithm's performance, yielding promising results that validate DRL as an effective solution for dynamic resource allocation.

We derive weighted $L^p$-Fourier-extension bounds for functions on the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ that are invariant under $O(N-k) \times O(k)$, extending the range of admissible exponents $p$ below the Stein-Tomas critical threshold $\frac{2(N+1)}{N-1}$. Furthermore, within the broader context of an arbitrary closed subgroup $G \subset O(N)$ and its invariant functions, we examine how weighted Fourier-extension estimates influence the boundedness and nonvanishing characteristics of the associated weighted Helmholtz resolvent operator. Leveraging these findings, we establish novel existence theorems for $G$-invariant solutions to the nonlinear Helmholtz equation
$$ - \Delta u - u = Q(x)|u|^{p-2}u, \quad u \in W^{2,p}(\mathbb{R}^{N}), $$
where $Q$ serves as a nonnegative, bounded weight function that remains invariant under $G$.

A primary objective of medical imaging is to accurately identify disease patterns unique to individual scans, yet brain imaging faces significant challenges due to the high heterogeneity in shape and appearance. Conventional approaches, which rely on registering images to a global template, often miss variable disease features because they prioritize population-based analyses suited for group averages rather than individual variations. Consequently, this paper leverages recent advancements in generative deep learning to create a method that performs simultaneous classification or regression alongside feature attribution (FA). We specifically investigate an ICAM VAE-GAN translation network designed to disentangle class-relevant features from background confounds, thereby enhancing interpretability and the regression of neurological phenotypes. Our method is validated on predicting Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort, as well as on brain age prediction for both neurodevelopment and neurodegeneration using the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) and UK Biobank datasets. We demonstrate that the generated FA maps effectively explain outlier predictions and confirm that incorporating a regression module improves latent space disentanglement. The source code is publicly accessible on Github at https://github.com/CherBass/ICAM.

We provide analytic solutions for two families of tennis-court integrals pertinent to $2\to2$ scattering processes with one massive external particle and massless propagators, expressed via Goncharov polylogarithms of transcendental weight up to six. Furthermore, we derive analytic results for physical kinematics for both the ladder-box and the two tennis-court families using real-valued polylogarithmic functions, thereby rendering our solutions ideal for phenomenological applications.

Tailoring the mechanical characteristics and light-matter interaction of solids requires precise control over their vibrations. Since thermal vibrations induce noise and dephasing in quantum processes, a viable approach involves engineering a phononic stop band—a frequency spectrum devoid of mechanical modes—to suppress these effects. In this study, we achieve the total elimination of mechanical vibrations at room temperature across a wide spectral range, featuring a 5.3 GHz band gap centered at 8.4 GHz within a patterned silicon nanostructure membrane, as verified by Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy. Furthermore, by implementing a line-defect waveguide, we directly observe GHz localized modes at ambient temperatures. These findings regarding thermally excited guided mechanical modes at the GHz scale offer a robust platform for photon-phonon integration, with significant implications for optomechanics and signal processing transduction.

Seismic image quality is fundamentally dependent on the precision of the velocity model, making the assessment of velocity errors through focusing analysis a crucial stage in seismic imaging workflows. Although analysis along the offset and aperture-angle axes is common, the physical (midpoint) axes are often overlooked because interpreting geological structures on these axes is complex and hard to automate. To address this, we have created an automatic, data-driven methodology leveraging convolutional neural networks to streamline image-focusing analysis. By applying focused and unfocused geological faults, we demonstrate that our technique effectively integrates both spatial and offset/angle focusing data to reliably estimate velocity errors. We further illustrate that our method successfully identifies velocity errors in a 2D Gulf of Mexico limited-aperture image where conventional semblance-based techniques fail. Additionally, our approach offers the advantage of enhancing fault interpretation within the seismic images.

This research investigates the Balanced Connected Subgraph (BCS) problem across various geometric intersection graphs, including interval, circular-arc, permutation, unit-disk, and outer-string graphs. In a vertex-colored graph $G=(V,E)$ where vertices are assigned either "red" or "blue" labels, the BCS problem aims to identify an induced connected subgraph $H$ with the largest possible number of vertices that maintains color balance, meaning it contains an equal count of red and blue vertices. We analyze the computational complexity of BCS within the context of these geometric graph classes. Specifically, we demonstrate that BCS is NP-hard for unit disk, outer-string, complete grid, and unit square graphs. Conversely, we develop polynomial-time algorithms to solve BCS on interval, circular-arc, and permutation graphs. Notably, our approach for the latter classes relies on a subroutine solving the Steiner Tree problem for both interval and circular arc graphs. Additionally, we introduce a Fixed-Parameter Tractable (FPT) algorithm applicable to general graphs.

We extend the optimized effective potential (OEP) framework within quantum electrodynamical density functional theory (QEDFT) to accommodate a continuous spectrum of photon modes, focusing on its utility for modeling the dissipative behavior of electron systems coupled to photons in lossy cavities. Our investigation specifically examines the method's ability to reproduce quantum aspects of electron-photon interactions, such as spontaneous emission and the associated energy transfer from electrons to cavity photons. To achieve this, we evaluate a minimal discrete three-site system comprising a single electron interacting with cavity photons; this setup effectively filters out classical radiation and associated energy loss while retaining nontrivial density dynamics. By analyzing two characteristic spectral densities of photon modes—specifically, (i) a lossy cavity featuring Lorentzian broadening of photon peaks and (ii) an Ohmic bath—across various representative dynamical regimes, we determine that OEP-QEDFT exhibits robust qualitative and quantitative accuracy, particularly when dissipation is governed primarily by one-photon processes.

This note develops regularity structures as a tool for addressing singular stochastic PDEs with non-translation invariant differential operators, specifically detailing the renormalised equation for a broad range of spacetime-dependent renormalization schemes.

This research investigates the solution front of the F-KPP equation featuring randomized non-linearity. Assuming the randomness satisfies conditions regarding spatial mixing and boundedness, we demonstrate that the solution's front lags behind the front of the corresponding linearized equation (the parabolic Anderson model) by no more than a logarithmic factor over time. This finding extends Bramson's results from the homogeneous case to a broader setting. Leveraging this result, we further derive functional central limit theorems for the fronts of solutions to both the F-KPP equation and the linearized model.

Measurements of radiofrequency emission from FTU plasmas containing runaway electrons (RE) within the 0.4–3 GHz range have achieved record-high time resolution. These observations capture rapid emission bursts linked to increased RE pitch-angle scattering, highlighting kinetic instabilities that drive the evolution of the RE population during its buildup phase. Additionally, such data serves as a sensitive indicator of instabilities in the early stages of RE formation. The sharp onset of radio bursts is significantly shorter than the intervening low-emission intervals, and spectral broadening during the growth phase suggests nonlinear wave coupling as the cause of this intermittency. Radiofrequency emission ceases at the start of post-disruption RE plateaus but returns as extremely intense bursts coinciding with strong increases in suprathermal electron cyclotron emission.

The bubble tree compactification for moduli spaces of anti-self-dual (ASD) Yang-Mills equations on $SU(2)$ or $SO(3)$ bundles over closed oriented Riemannian 4-manifolds $M$ was established in [T88], [F95], [C02], [C10], [F14], and [F15], with the smooth orbifold structure away from the trivial stratum detailed in [C02] and [C10]. This paper extends that methodology to 4-orbifolds of the form $M/\mathbb{Z}_\alpha$ satisfying Condition \ref{the assumption of group action in this thesis}, thereby deriving a bubble tree compactification for the instanton moduli space on these specific 4-orbifolds.

This Letter introduces a strategy for synchronizing an arbitrary set of nodes within a directed network to follow a trajectory that is generally distinct from that of the remaining network units. This problem is motivated by natural and artificial systems where optimal operation relies on clusters of synchronizing nodes. Our approach utilizes distributed controllers that alter network topology to induce outer symmetries among the targeted nodes. Additionally, we formulate an optimization problem for selecting these controllers—encompassing the minimization of added or removed links—and provide an algorithm to solve it.

Although robotic assembly and disassembly significantly enhance the financial efficiency and environmental sustainability of industrial operations, they remain underexplored in current literature, a gap that contradicts their pivotal role in the Fourth Industrial Revolution. While existing research extensively addresses the optimization of assembly and disassembly for specific products, it frequently neglects other critical factors, such as the types of robots utilized in sequence plans across the entire lifecycle—including design, assembly, disassembly, and reassembly. Isolating these operations from the broader ecosystem components risks leading to flawed conclusions regarding both the necessity and efficiency of these procedures. This paper aims to address these deficiencies by comprehensively reviewing the state-of-the-art in robotic assembly and disassembly, examining various manufacturing and remanufacturing frameworks with a specific focus on their potential to support a circular economy.

This work investigates the periodic complex action theory (CAT) by applying a periodic constraint to the future-included CAT framework, where time integration proceeds from the past toward the future. We extend the concept of the weak value—a normalized matrix element of an operator $\hat{\mathcal O}$ from real action theory—to a new expression denoted as $\langle \hat{\mathcal O} \rangle_{\mathrm{periodic}~\mathrm{time}}$. We establish two theorems demonstrating that this expression yields a real value for Hermitian operators $\hat{\mathcal O}$ when evaluated using a modified inner product that renders a specific non-normal Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$ normal. The first theorem applies to a fixed period $t_p$ under the condition that exactly one eigenstate possesses the maximal imaginary part $B$ of the eigenvalues of $\hat{H}$. The second theorem concerns a period $t_p$ chosen to maximize the absolute transition amplitude, applicable when $B \leq 0$ and $|B|$ is significantly smaller than the spacing between any two real parts of the eigenvalues of $\hat{H}$. The latter result, derived through number-theoretical reasoning, implies that if the universe is periodic, the period itself may function as an adjustable parameter determined within the Feynman path integral. This represents a variant of the maximization principle previously introduced by the authors.

This study establishes existence and orbital stability properties for periodic standing waves within the cubic-quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. By applying the implicit function theorem, we construct a smooth curve of explicit periodic waves featuring a \textit{dnoidal} profile; this construction demonstrates that the associated period map is strictly increasing with respect to energy levels. Furthermore, this monotonicity aids in analyzing the non-positive spectrum of the linearized operator near the wave. Regarding stability, we show that these \textit{dnoidal} waves are orbitally stable in the energy space when restricted to even functions.

This paper investigates unsupervised multi-hop reranking for open-domain multi-hop question answering (MQA). Because MQA involves synthesizing information across multiple documents, the primary difficulty lies in retrieving and reranking chains of passages that facilitate the reasoning process. Our proposed method, LEPUS (LargE models with Prompt-Utilizing reranking Strategy), employs instruction-like prompts derived from candidate document paths to calculate a path's relevance score as the likelihood of generating a specific question, leveraging a pre-trained language model. Despite being unsupervised, LEPUS achieves reranking performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods trained on thousands of examples. Furthermore, incorporating a minimal number of samples (e.g., two) via in-context learning yields additional performance improvements. Finally, we demonstrate that integrating LEPUS with a reader module enables competitive multi-hop QA results, surpassing even fully-supervised QA systems. The code will be made available at https://github.com/mukhal/LEPUS.

This study tackles the determined audio source separation problem within the time-frequency domain. While Independent Deeply Learned Matrix Analysis (IDLMA) assumes zero inter-frequency correlation for each source spectrum—a limitation when modeling nonstationary signals like music—Independent Positive Semidefinite Tensor Analysis was introduced to address frequency correlations. However, this unsupervised approach overly constrains the structure of frequency covariance matrices (FCMs) to minimize model parameters. Extending these conventional methods, we propose a supervised technique that utilizes deep neural networks (DNNs) to model FCMs. Since directly inferring FCMs via DNNs is challenging, we introduce a novel FCM model defined as a convex combination of a diagonal FCM and a rank-1 FCM. This flexible model effectively captures both inter-frequency correlations and the dynamics of time-varying FCMs inherent in nonstationary signals. We estimate the proposed FCMs using two distinct DNNs: one for power spectrum estimation and another for time-domain signal estimation. Experimental results on music signal separation demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to IDLMA.

Quantum computing leverages specific quantum phenomena for information processing and is often celebrated as the next generation of computing, yet it faces significant obstacles in practical implementation. MemComputing represents an emerging paradigm that utilizes non-quantum dynamical systems and leverages time non-locality (memory) to perform computations. It can be efficiently simulated in software, and its transition to hardware appears more direct. This discussion will explore both the similarities and the key distinctions between these two computational approaches.

A strong Gelfand pair (G,H) consists of a group G and a subgroup H where every irreducible character of H induces a multiplicity-free character on G. This paper classifies the strong Gelfand pairs for the special linear groups SL(2, p), where p denotes a prime number.

This paper investigates isolated singular solutions to the semilinear Helmholtz equation $-\Delta u-u=Q|u|^{p-1}u$ defined on $\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}$, subject to the condition $\lim_{|x|\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, where $N\geq 2$, $p>1$, and the potential $Q: \mathbb{R}^N\to (0,+\infty)$ is Hölder continuous with specific decay properties at infinity. We classify the isolated singularity within Serrin's subcritical regime and derive the form of these solutions as $u_k=k\Phi+v_k$ using the Schauder fixed point theorem applied to the integral equation $v_k=\Phi\ast\big(Q|kw_\sigma+v_k|^{p-1}(kw_\sigma+v_k)\big)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. In this context, $\Phi$ represents the real-valued fundamental solution for $-\Delta-1$, and $w_\sigma$ denotes a real-valued solution to $(-\Delta-1)w_\sigma=\delta_0$ whose behavior at infinity is bounded by $|x|^{-\sigma}$ for some $\sigma\leq \frac{N-1}{2}$.

Despite organizations' ongoing efforts to secure critical infrastructure against network attacks through air-gapping, adversaries continuously evolve, discovering covert channels to leak data from isolated systems. For example, researchers have proven that data can be extracted from computers inside Faraday cages by manipulating magnetic fields. While recent literature has explored various physical covert channels, these attacks have predominantly targeted open-loop cyber-physical systems where the physical pathways remain unmonitored. In contrast, architectures like fog computing transmit sensitive information to cyber-physical edge devices, whose physical side channels are typically safeguarded by state estimation techniques. This paper formally addresses covert data exfiltration by leveraging existing cyber-physical models and device infrastructure to bypass stealthily. Specifically, we propose a method to evade cyber-physical state estimation intrusion detection systems while extracting sensitive data. We introduce a generalized framework for encoding and decoding sensitive information within cyber-physical control loops. Our approach is evaluated on a distributed IoT network featuring computation nodes on physical drones and an industrial control system managing a robotic arm. Unlike previous studies, we rigorously define the constraints of covert exfiltration in cyber-physical channels when a defender actively performs state estimation.

This work establishes the integral Chow and cohomology rings for the moduli stack $\mathcal{B}_{r,d}$, which classifies rank $r$, degree $d$ vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$. We begin by demonstrating that the rational Chow ring $A_{\mathbb{Q}}^*(\mathcal{B}_{r,d})$ constitutes a free $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra generated by $2r+1$ elements, a structure whose isomorphism class remains invariant regardless of $d$. Subsequently, we prove that the integral Chow ring $A^*(\mathcal{B}_{r,d})$ is torsion-free and identify multiplicative generators for it as a subring of $A_{\mathbb{Q}}^*(\mathcal{B}_{r,d})$. These findings reveal that $A^*(\mathcal{B}_{r,d})$ cannot be finitely generated as a $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra. Finally, we show that the cohomology ring of $\mathcal{B}_{r,d}$ is isomorphic to its Chow ring.

Conducting network algorithm tests in physical environments with actual hardware is crucial for narrowing the divide between theoretical models and practical application, particularly when investigating technologies like Bluetooth Mesh. We developed a data collection approach for Bluetooth Mesh and deployed it across both indoor and outdoor scenarios using ESP-32 microcontrollers. This strategy also evaluated an alternative packet routing method based on Bluetooth Mesh - MAM, which had previously been simulated using the OMNET++ simulator. A comparison between these real-world ESP-32 experiments and prior simulations revealed significant discrepancies: the simulations forecasted a +459% increase in unique message collection, whereas the ESP-32 tests yielded different results. These findings highlighted substantial opportunities for enhancing our ESP-32 implementation in future work, specifically addressing an unforeseen issue with packet duplication in the MAM algorithm. Despite this, the MAM strategy outperformed Bluetooth Mesh's default relay mechanism, collecting up to 4.06% more unique data messages. Additionally, we outline several challenges encountered during the implementation, deployment, and benchmarking of Bluetooth Mesh on the ESP-32 platform.

Audio-visual speech enhancement systems represent a highly promising approach for isolating and improving the speech of a target speaker. Conventional techniques typically rely on naive encoder-decoder architectures based on convolutional neural networks to predict clean speech spectra; however, these methods suffer from two main limitations: they fail to utilize data comprehensively and struggle to effectively balance audio-visual features. The proposed model addresses these issues by implementing a mechanism that fuses audio and visual features layer-by-layer during the encoding phase, subsequently feeding these integrated features to corresponding decoder layers. Furthermore, it introduces a two-stage multi-head cross-attention (MHCA) mechanism to optimize the balance of fused features while filtering out irrelevant information. This study presents an attentional audio-visual multi-layer feature fusion model, where MHCA units are integrated into the feature mapping at every decoder layer. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed network achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art models.

In physical sciences, sensor measurements gathered over time generate time series data. However, real-world conditions and sensor physics often introduce noise. Additionally, sampling rate limitations prevent the collection of data at every time point, necessitating interpolation. Standard interpolation techniques may lack smoothness, fail to remove noise, and result in poor derivatives that obscure high-order dynamics. To address these issues, this article proposes employing an AutoEncoder for simultaneous interpolation and denoising, supported by a practical real-world example.

We introduce a hierarchical Green function method based on multi-site correlation functions to investigate the properties of a 2D square lattice Hubbard model. This approach involves solving the equations of motion for a one-particle Green function alongside its associated multi-site correlations. By applying a cutoff approximation and utilizing the Fourier representation of these correlations, we derive an analytical expression for the one-particle Green function that incorporates static correlation functions. Consequently, we calculate the electron spectral density function, revealing two primary peaks corresponding to the lower and upper Hubbard bands. Additionally, we identify novel states situated between these peaks, with their total spectral weight scaling proportionally to the hole doping concentration. Furthermore, the emergence of collective modes suggests possible charge/spin density wave and/or electronic pairing density wave ordering. These findings align perfectly with spectroscopic observations of cuprate superconductors in their normal states. Moreover, the inclusion of static correlation functions within the one-particle Green function offers a framework for describing the intertwined orders characteristic of the normal state in cuprate superconductors.

Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is often degraded by severe speckle, a spatially correlated and signal-dependent noise that can impede image analysis. Removing this noise through despeckling is crucial for enhancing the performance of subsequent image processing tasks. While initial despeckling techniques emerged in the 1970s with various model-based algorithms, the field has gained significant momentum due to the advent of powerful deep learning models, which have proven highly effective for inverse problems in image processing. This paper reviews the literature on deep learning approaches for SAR despeckling, encompassing both supervised and recent self-supervised methods. We offer a critical evaluation of current techniques to highlight promising research directions, pinpoint limitations hindering the success of deep models, and suggest future pathways to fully leverage deep learning for SAR despeckling.

This study investigates an expanding two-fluid model comprising non-relativistic dark matter and radiation, which interact temporarily to reach approximate thermal equilibrium. This interaction produces an effective bulk viscous pressure at the background level, a phenomenon expected to be significant during the transition from radiation to matter dominance. We calculate the magnitude of this pressure for dark matter masses between $1 {\rm eV}$ and $10 {\rm eV}$ near the matter-radiation equality epoch (redshift $z_{\rm eq}\sim 3400$). Our results show that this transient bulk viscosity has implications for resolving current tensions in the standard cosmological model: i) the additional negative pressure alters the expansion rate around $z_{\rm eq}$, resulting in a higher $H_0$ value, and ii) large-scale structure formation is affected by a new viscous friction term in the Mészáros effect, which suppresses the growth of matter overdensity amplitudes. Consequently, both the $H_0$ and $S_8$ tensions within the standard cosmological framework are substantially alleviated.

Investigating the physical mechanisms driving star formation represents a central challenge in contemporary astrophysics. The Cosmic Infrared Background (CIB), generated by the cumulative emission from dusty star-forming galaxies since the reionization era, serves as a vital complementary tool for reconstructing star formation history and acts as a significant extragalactic foreground in Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) research. Consequently, deciphering the physics behind the CIB is crucial for advancing both cosmological models and theories of galaxy formation. This study presents high signal-to-noise measurements of the cross-correlation between CIB maps from the Planck mission and cosmic shear data from the Dark Energy Survey and Kilo-Degree Survey. Since cosmic shear, primarily arising from the weak gravitational lensing of background galaxy photons, provides a direct map of matter distribution, its correlation with the CIB allows for a direct test of the relationship between star formation rate (SFR) density and matter density. By analyzing these measurements, we constrain a halo-based SFR model that describes the efficiency of gas-to-star conversion as a function of halo mass and redshift. These results are strengthened by integrating them with model-independent measurements of bias-weighted SFR density derived from the tomographic cross-correlation of galaxies and the CIB. Our analysis yields constraints on the peak efficiency at low redshifts, $\eta=0.445^{+0.055}_{-0.11}$, and on the halo mass where this peak occurs today, $\log_{10}(M_1/M_\odot) = 12.17\pm0.25$. These findings align exceptionally well with direct SFR density measurements and other investigations utilizing the CIB.

A novel covariant density functional, PCF-PK1, is introduced, characterized by local exchange terms within four-fermion interactions derived via Fierz transformation. Its coupling constants are fixed using empirical saturation data, the ab initio equation of state, proton-neutron Dirac mass splittings in nuclear matter, and ground-state characteristics of specific spherical nuclei. The efficacy of PCF-PK1 is demonstrated through its description of infinite nuclear matter and finite nuclei, covering ground-state properties and Gamow-Teller resonances. Notably, PCF-PK1 resolves spurious shell closures at Z = 58 and Z = 92, a common flaw in many covariant density functionals lacking exchange terms. Furthermore, Gamow-Teller resonances are accurately reproduced without adjustable parameters, confirming that localized exchange terms enable a self-consistent description of these resonances within the PCF-PK1 framework.

Theoretical analysis is employed to derive fission characteristics of actinide nuclei, focusing on potential energy surfaces and fission barriers to forecast fission fragment mass-yields for various actinide isotopes. Where possible, these findings are validated against experimental data. The computations utilize the macroscopic-microscopic approach, combining the Lublin-Strasbourg Drop (LSD) model for the macroscopic component with microscopic energy corrections derived from the Yukawa-folded potential. Nuclear shapes, including non-axial degrees of freedom, are modeled using Fourier nuclear shape parametrization. Finally, the mass-yields of fission fragments for the studied nuclei are calculated within a 3D collective framework based on the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.

We introduce Citrinet, a novel end-to-end automatic speech recognition (ASR) system based on convolutional Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC). As a deep residual neural network, Citrinet integrates 1D time-channel separable convolutions with sub-word encoding and squeeze-and-excitation mechanisms. This architecture substantially narrows the performance gap between non-autoregressive models and both sequence-to-sequence and transducer approaches. Evaluated on the LibriSpeech, TED-LIUM2, AISHELL-1, and Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS) English datasets, Citrinet achieves accuracy comparable to the leading autoregressive Transducer models.

We demonstrate that knots and links possessing an irreducible diagram with three high twists and more than two twist regions are hyperbolic. This finding parallels the result by Futer and Purcell regarding 6-highly twisted diagrams. Although their approach relies on geometric techniques, our proof establishes hyperbolicity by proving that the complements of these knots or links are both unannular and atoroidal. We achieve this through a novel method utilizing an Euler characteristic argument.

Hierarchical strategic decision-making is ubiquitous across large organizations and decentralized political structures. To formally model these interactions, we propose a new category of structured hierarchical games (SHGs). In an SHG, players correspond to nodes within a tree, where decision-making proceeds sequentially from the root down to the leaves: the root moves first, followed by its children, and so on. A player's utility function relies on their own action, the decisions of their parent, and the outcomes of all leaf nodes. This framework extends both simultaneous-move games and multi-follower Stackelberg games. By exploiting the sequential nature of moves and the specific payoff dependencies, we developed a gradient-based algorithm resembling back propagation, termed Differential Backward Induction (DBI), to approximate SHG equilibria. We establish a sufficient condition for DBI's convergence and validate its effectiveness in identifying approximate equilibrium solutions for various hierarchical policy-making models.

This study investigates the decays $B^{0}_{s}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}$ and $B^{0}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}$ using data from proton-proton collisions with an integrated luminosity of 3 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb detector in 2011 and 2012. The analysis reconstructs the $\tau$ lepton via the $\tau^{-}\to\pi^{-}\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\nu_{\tau}$ decay channel. No significant signal is detected. Under the assumption that no $B^{0}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}$ decays contribute, an upper limit of $\mathcal{B}\left( B^{0}_{s}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}\right) < 4.2\times 10^{-5}$ is established at the 95% confidence level. Conversely, assuming no $B^{0}_{s}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}$ contribution yields a limit of $\mathcal{B}\left( B^{0}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}\right) < 1.4\times 10^{-5}$ at 95% confidence level. These results represent the first constraint on the branching fraction of $B^{0}_{s}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}$ and the most stringent limit available globally for $B^{0}\to\tau^{\pm}\mu^{\mp}$.

This manuscript introduces a new dark energy model designed to investigate the fundamental nature of dark energy. The study relies primarily on non-extensive Kaniadakis entropy and a timescale acting as an infrared cutoff, with the age of the Universe serving as the specific cutoff metric. We examine the cosmological properties of this proposed model, analyzing the evolution of a universe containing pressure-free matter alongside various dark energy candidates. Both interacting and non-interacting scenarios between these two sectors are considered. We derive the differential equation for the dark energy density parameter, along with the expressions for the equation of state and deceleration parameters. The analysis of the deceleration parameter indicates a transition from a decelerated to an accelerated phase at approximately $z\approx 0.6$. Furthermore, the squared sound speed is plotted against redshift $z$ to assess the stability of the model under both conditions.

Moore digraphs, characterized by an out-degree $d$, diameter $k$, and order matching the Moore bound $M(d,k) = 1 + d + d^2 + \dots +d^k$, are central to the study of optimal network designs. To explore structures resembling Moore digraphs, recent research has focused on small digraphs with minimum out-degree $d$ where at most one directed path of length $\leq k$ exists between any pair of vertices $u$ and $v$; these graphs possess an order of $M(d,k)+\epsilon$, where $\epsilon$ represents a small excess. Sillasen et al. demonstrated that no such digraphs exist with an out-degree of two and an excess of one. The current author has classified all digraphs with an out-degree of two and an excess of two. This paper establishes that no diregular digraphs with an out-degree of two and an excess of three exist for $k \geq 3$, marking the first classification of digraphs with an order three greater than the Moore bound for a fixed out-degree.

We demonstrate that various distinct broken-symmetry phases in an easy-plane anisotropic spin-1/2 anti-ferromagnet on a square lattice—specifically the valence bond solid, chiral spin liquid, and XY-ordered states—can all be reached by perturbing a multi-critical point characterized by two massless Dirac fermions interacting with a level-one Chern-Simons gauge field. This framework offers a unified perspective on these phases and the transitions connecting them. Furthermore, our analysis of a particular phase transition provides a lattice realization of a recently proposed fermion-boson duality, thereby supporting the hypothesis. We also briefly examine the connection between our findings and the long-anticipated de-confined criticality in such systems.

Despite their significant success, Vision Transformers (ViTs) struggle with resolution scalability, experiencing sharp performance declines when encountering input resolutions not seen during training. To address this, we present ResFormer, a framework leveraging multi-resolution training to enhance performance across a broad spectrum of testing resolutions, many of which remain unseen. ResFormer processes replicated images at varying resolutions and applies a scale consistency loss to facilitate interactive information exchange across different scales. Crucially, we introduce a global-local positional embedding strategy that adapts smoothly based on input dimensions, enabling the model to effectively handle novel resolutions. Extensive experiments on ImageNet image classification demonstrate that ResFormer possesses robust scaling capabilities. For example, ResFormer-B-MR achieves Top-1 accuracies of 75.86% and 81.72% on low (96) and high (640) resolutions, respectively, outperforming DeiT-B by 48% and 7.49%. Additionally, we show that ResFormer is versatile and can be readily extended to tasks such as semantic segmentation and video action recognition.

In the majority of Swiss municipalities, non-recyclable waste is collected via a curbside system where heavy trucks visit nearly every household. This frequent stopping pattern results in elevated fuel usage, emissions, and noise levels. These negative impacts can be mitigated by decreasing the number of stops made by collection vehicles. One effective strategy involves establishing collection points across the municipality, allowing residents to deposit waste at their preferred locations. The associated optimization challenge requires selecting a subset of candidate sites so that every household can dispose of its waste at its most favored location. Given an available road network, this specific problem is termed the Capacitated Multi-Vehicle Covering Tour Problem on a Road Network (Cm-CTP-R). We present two Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) models: one leveraging the sparsity of the road network and another, customer-based formulation common in Vehicle Routing Problems (VRP). To handle large-scale instances, we develop a two-phase heuristic that tackles the two underlying subproblems of the Cm-CTP-R: a set covering problem for site selection and a split-delivery VRP for route planning. Computational tests on both small and real-world datasets indicate that the road-network-based formulation performs superiorly. Additionally, the proposed heuristic yields high-quality solutions, achieving optimality gaps under 0.5% and 3.5% for 75% of small and real-life instances, respectively, and often outperforms exact methods on larger real-world cases.

This paper demonstrates that the stability analysis presented in "A note on stability of fractional logistic maps," *Appl. Math. Lett.* 125 (2022) 107787, is flawed and provides a reproof of a theorem regarding the convergence of a convolution formed by the product of a converging series and a converging sequence. Furthermore, we note that the aforementioned paper should have undergone more rigorous editing.

We establish the existence of global-in-time solutions for the semilinear equation describing spin-1/2 particles within the Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker spacetime, assuming small initial data. Furthermore, we demonstrate that if the initial function adheres to the Lochak-Majorana condition, global solutions persist even for arbitrarily large initial values. These solutions scatter toward free solutions as time progresses. The mass term is treated as complex-valued, and we analyze constraints on its imaginary component by proving that global solutions fail to exist when specific relationships between the scale function and the mass are met.

This work investigates Liouville-type theorems and the asymptotic behavior of positive solutions near an isolated singular point $\zeta \in \partial\Omega\cup\{\infty\}$ for the quasilinear elliptic equation $$-\text{div}(|\nabla u|_A^{p-2}A\nabla u)+V|u|^{p-2}u =0\quad\text{ in } \Omega,$$ defined on a domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\geq 2$ and $1<p<d$. The coefficient matrix $A=(a_{ij})$, which belongs to $L_{\rm loc}^{\infty}(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^{d\times d})$, is assumed to be symmetric and locally uniformly positive definite. Furthermore, the potential $V$ is taken from a specific Wolff class and exhibits a generalized Fuchsian-type singularity at the isolated point $\zeta\in \partial \Omega \cup \{\infty\}$. These properties are analyzed using scaling arguments and Harnack's inequality.

We demonstrate the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions across all Fano threefolds by establishing a modified version of a conjecture proposed by Bayer, Toda, and the second author. A crucial component of this proof is a robust Bogomolov inequality, recently established by Chunyi Li. Furthermore, we verify the original conjecture for certain toric threefolds by employing the toric Frobenius morphism.

ABIDE stands as the most extensive open-source repository for autism spectrum disorder, offering comprehensive fMRI datasets alongside detailed phenotypic profiles. While prior research has extensively analyzed these data using functional connectivity and deep learning on raw inputs—achieving model accuracies near 75% across distinct scanning sites—challenges persist regarding the transferability of models between different sites within ABIDE. This paper introduces, for the first time, domain adaptation techniques applied to brain pathology classification using raw neuroimaging data. By employing 3D convolutional autoencoders to construct a domain-agnostic latent space image representation, we demonstrate that this approach surpasses existing methods when evaluated on ABIDE data.

Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) have recently attracted significant attention in the computer vision community due to their ability to generate photorealistic novel views of real-world scenes. However, a key limitation of NeRF is its dependence on precise camera poses to learn scene representations. To address this, we introduce Bundle-Adjusting Neural Radiance Fields (BARF), a method designed to train NeRF using imperfect or even unknown camera poses by jointly optimizing neural 3D representations and registering camera frames.
