Building on prior research that derived and validated closed-form solutions for the rocking response of slender blocks, these proposed laws are verified through detailed numerical simulations that account for combined rocking, up-lifting, and sliding mechanisms in monolithic structures. The application of these laws to multi-drum stone columns is also examined, demonstrating that despite complex behaviors such as wobbling and impacts, similarity is maintained. These developments confirm the applicability of the proposed scaling laws for designing reduced-scale experiments of masonry structures.

Over recent years, the Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has expanded substantially, forming a vast repository of research that offers numerous opportunities for statistical analysis across various facets of theorem proving, though these potential applications remain largely untapped. Yet, this expansion introduces specific challenges, as locating materials becomes progressively more difficult while the need for reusability and clarity grows. This thesis abstract outlines my research agenda focused on these issues and briefly highlights preliminary findings suggesting that the dependency graph of the archive exhibits a scale-free distribution in terms of node in-degree.

CycleGAN has recently demonstrated high-performance, ultra-fast denoising for low-dose X-ray CT without requiring paired training data, a feat made possible by cycle consistency. However, the standard CycleGAN framework necessitates two generators and two discriminators to enforce this consistency, resulting in high GPU consumption and demanding training expertise. While a recent adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN)-based tunable CycleGAN partially addresses this by utilizing a single generator, it still relies on two discriminators and an extra AdaIN code generator. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel cycle-free CycleGAN architecture featuring only one generator and one discriminator while maintaining cycle consistency. This innovation stems from the insight that an invertible generator inherently satisfies the cycle consistency condition, thereby removing the need for the second discriminator. To enhance the efficacy of this invertible generator, the network operates within the wavelet residual domain. Comprehensive experiments across various low-dose CT noise levels demonstrate that our approach significantly boosts denoising performance while utilizing merely 10% of the learnable parameters and achieving faster training speeds compared to conventional CycleGAN.

A four-dimensional Chern-Simons modification of general relativity is examined using the Gitman-Lyakhovich-Tyutin canonical analysis tailored for higher-order theories. This study details the enumeration of physical degrees of freedom, identifies the relevant symmetries, and presents the fundamental Dirac brackets. Furthermore, the full structure of the constraints is outlined, and their corresponding Dirac algebra is constructed.

Numerous model watermarking approaches have been created to protect deployed commercial models from covert theft via model distillation. However, watermarks generated by most current methods are vulnerable to ensemble distillation, as averaging the outputs of multiple models can substantially diminish or completely eliminate the watermark. This paper addresses the difficult challenge of defending against ensemble distillation by introducing a new technique called CosWM. CosWM is designed with elegance and offers strong theoretical guarantees, delivering superior watermarking performance against ensemble attacks. Extensive experiments on public datasets confirm CosWM's effectiveness and its advantages over state-of-the-art baselines.

We established the largest database for kinship recognition, labeling it with a novel clustering algorithm that utilized label proposals as side information to enhance cluster accuracy, resulting in significant reductions in time and manual effort. Statistically, FIW demonstrates substantial improvements over previous datasets. We have introduced multiple benchmarks for kinship verification, family classification, tri-subject verification, and large-scale search and retrieval. Additionally, CNNs trained on FIW were deployed on the KinWild I and II datasets to achieve state-of-the-art results. Most recently, FIW was augmented with MM, enabling kinship recognition systems to leverage video dynamics, audio, and text captions in their decision-making processes. We anticipate that FIW will have a profound impact on both research and practical applications. Furthermore, we addressed the classic problem of facial landmark localization. Many existing networks rely on L1 or L2 norm objectives, which suffer from limitations: landmark locations are derived from heatmaps where predicted positions are penalized without considering the spread, meaning high scatter indicates low confidence and vice versa. To resolve this, we introduced an objective function that penalizes low-confidence predictions. We also tackled the issue of reliance on expensive, error-prone labeled data. Our solution involves an adversarial training framework that utilizes unlabeled data to boost model performance. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on renowned benchmarks, while maintaining robustness with a significantly reduced size—using one-eighth the number of channels yet performing comparably to state-of-the-art models in real-time on a CPU. Finally, we developed BFW as a proxy to measure bias across ethnicity and gender subgroups, allowing for the characterization of face recognition performance per subgroup. Our findings indicate that performance is suboptimal when a single threshold is used to determine the genuineness of sample pairs.

Deep learning architectures are increasingly being applied to tabular data, with TabTransformer currently serving as a state-of-the-art solution by utilizing an attention mechanism to capture relationships among categorical features and a standard MLP to generate final logits. This paper introduces several modifications to the original TabTransformer that achieve superior performance on binary classification tasks across three distinct datasets, yielding over 1% improvements in AUROC. Drawing inspiration from gated MLPs, we implement linear projections within the MLP block and evaluate multiple activation functions. Furthermore, we assess the significance of various hyperparameters during the training process.

This study introduces a new class of interacting vacuum models by reformulating the equation of state from lattice kinetic theory, originally proposed by Shan and Chen, as the interaction between the vacuum and cold dark matter (CDM). This interaction drives vacuum evolution and exhibits nonlinearity around a characteristic energy scale, $\rho_*$, transitioning to a linear coupling with power-law evolution at scales significantly lower or higher than $\rho_*$. Concentrating on the simplest subclass where interactions involve solely energy exchange and CDM follows geodesic motion, we first explore various models derived from the Shan--Chen coupling, demonstrating diverse behaviors at early and late times contingent on parameter choices. Subsequently, we impose the first observational constraints on this Shan--Chen interacting vacuum framework through an MCMC analysis to identify model and cosmological parameters favored by data. We prioritize models where coupling nonlinearity is significant at late times, setting the reference scale $\rho_*$ equal to the critical energy density of $\Lambda$CDM. Our results indicate that observational data are consistent with a broad spectrum of models yielding distinct cosmologies; however, $\Lambda$CDM remains preferred over all examined Shan--Chen interacting vacuum scenarios. Furthermore, we note that these models fail to alleviate the $H_0$ and $\sigma_8$ tensions.

I present a comprehensive unified framework integrating particle physics and cosmology, grounded in an extended standard particle model and the foundational principles of standard cosmology. This model successfully explains the shared origins of inflation, reheating, baryon asymmetry, dark matter, dark energy, and neutrino mass. It provides a coherent and complete characterization of the universe's entire evolution, spanning primordial inflation, early reheating, baryogenesis, the subsequent hot expansion, and the current transition from cold dark matter condensation to dark energy. For every evolutionary stage, I derive the complete dynamical system of equations and solve them using specialized techniques, thereby establishing intrinsic links between these cosmic processes and particle physics. Numerical results demonstrate the successful implementation of this approach. Despite relying on only seven input parameters, the model perfectly replicates observed inflationary data and the present energy density budget, while accurately predicting the inflaton mass ($M_{\Delta}\approx6.26\times10^{10}$ GeV), CDM mass ($m_{S}\approx0.30$ KeV), baryon-to-photon ratio ($\eta_{B}\approx6.08\times10^{-10}$), and the Hubble parameter ($h\approx0.674$). Ultimately, this unified model holds significant promise for experimental verification in the near future.

We introduce a clinical data analysis workflow grounded in Bayesian Structure Learning (BSL), an unsupervised method resilient to noise and bias. This approach integrates prior medical knowledge to generate explainable outputs in the form of causal graphs illustrating connections among features. The process follows a multi-step trajectory: first, BSL identifies the primary drivers of patient outcomes; second, a Binary Decision Tree (BDT) tool is developed for clinical use to flag high-risk patients using data available at hospital admission. Evaluated on a comprehensive COVID-19 dataset, our framework offers a schematic overview of the multi-factorial processes influencing patient outcomes, aligning with current pathogenic understanding. Furthermore, the method produces a highly interpretable tool that accurately predicts outcomes for 85% of subjects using only three admission features: age, history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and the PaO2/FiO2 ratio. Predictive accuracy rises to 94.5% when augmented with four additional routine blood tests: Creatinine, Glucose, pO2, and Sodium.

This study examines the combined execution of reservation and de-reservation policies within India, a nation that has upheld comprehensive affirmative action since 1950. A pivotal 2008 Supreme Court ruling required that unfilled OBC seats (accounting for 27% of the quota) be filled by general category applicants in public schools, yet it failed to specify an implementation method. We highlight the deficiencies in the recently revised allocation process for technical college admissions and propose a solution utilizing de-reservation through specific choice rules. Our approach introduces a new priority design called the Backward Transfers (BT) choice rule for institutions, paired with a Deferred Acceptance mechanism under these rules (DA-BT) for centralized clearinghouses. We demonstrate that the DA-BT mechanism rectifies the flaws of current systems. Furthermore, by translating India's legal mandates and policy objectives into formal axioms, we prove that the DA-BT mechanism is the sole solution for simultaneously implementing both reservation and de-reservation policies.

This technical report offers theoretical assurances regarding the recursive feasibility and practical exponential stability of a closed-loop system involving a feedback linearizable nonlinear system under a robust data-driven nonlinear predictive control strategy. Serving as supplementary material to our recent publication, "Data-based control of feedback linearizable systems," the arguments presented mirror the approach used for linear time-invariant (LTI) systems, leveraging the fact that feedback linearizable systems exhibit linearity in transformed coordinates. Nevertheless, the proof has been appropriately modified to align with the specific nonlinear context, with these distinctions highlighted throughout the demonstration.

Big data analytics (BDA) applications leverage machine learning algorithms to derive meaningful insights from vast, rapid, and diverse data sources. However, BDA development faces new software engineering hurdles, particularly in maintaining algorithmic performance despite the 3Vs: volume, velocity, and variety. The inherent complexity of BDA software often results in protracted development cycles, delayed deployments, and difficult performance evaluations. To address these issues, this paper introduces a Domain-Specific Model (DSM) alongside DevOps practices for designing, deploying, and monitoring performance metrics within BDA applications. The proposed solution encompasses a design methodology and a framework that utilizes integrated high-level abstractions to specify architectural inputs, software components, and deployment strategies, thereby facilitating Quality of Service (QoS) monitoring. We validated this approach across four use cases spanning various domains to demonstrate its broad applicability. Our findings indicate that this method achieves reduced deployment and monitoring durations, along with a higher gain factor per iteration compared to existing solutions.

Current deep learning approaches for compressive sensing reconstruction are often limited by the opaque nature of deep neural networks (DNNs). To address this, we introduce CSMCNet, an interpretable deep network designed for motion estimation. By unfolding the iterative optimization steps of traditional algorithms, CSMCNet achieves high-quality video compressive sensing reconstruction. Our method incorporates a DNN-based multi-hypothesis motion estimation module to enhance reconstruction fidelity, alongside a residual module that minimizes the discrepancy between the reconstructed output and the original signal. Additionally, we propose an interpolation module with a dedicated training strategy to enable scalable compressive sensing, allowing a single model to handle various compression ratios. Experimental results demonstrate a PSNR of 29.34 dB at a 2% compressive ratio (98% compression), outperforming existing state-of-the-art techniques. Furthermore, the interpolation module proves effective, delivering substantial cost reductions with only acceptable performance trade-offs.

Inspired by regulator theory and adaptive control, various concepts of output stability within the input-to-state stability (ISS) framework were established for finite-dimensional systems. These notions are fundamentally distinct, as they capture different ways state variables influence the transient behavior of outputs. This paper extends the investigation of these output stability properties to delay systems. Our primary goal is to elucidate the relationships among these various notions in the context of delay systems and to derive corresponding Razumikhin criteria. Furthermore, these findings are pivotal for formulating converse Lyapunov theorems regarding output stability for such systems.

Lack of labeled data for neural network training is frequently mitigated by incorporating task-specific knowledge, which often yields heuristic yet noisy labels. This knowledge is encoded in labeling functions that identify patterns within training samples to assign annotations. However, such weakly supervised approaches can lead to an excessive dependence on the signals provided by these functions, preventing models from utilizing alternative cues or achieving robust generalization. We introduce KnowMAN, an adversarial framework designed to regulate the impact of signals tied to specific labeling functions. By compelling the network to learn representations that remain invariant to these specific signals while focusing on more general indicators of output labels, KnowMAN significantly outperforms direct weakly supervised learning methods, including those utilizing pre-trained transformer language models and feature-based baselines.

Achieving high-quality imaging typically demands large, costly lenses to mitigate geometric and chromatic aberrations, creating significant barriers for optical hash or budget-friendly applications. While algorithmic reconstruction can theoretically eliminate artifacts from low-end optics, the spatially varying nature of these aberrations forces a compromise between computational efficiency and performance. High-quality restoration often requires computationally intensive strategies, such as patch-wise optimization or training extensive sets of localized deep neural networks. This paper introduces a PSF-aware plug-and-play deep network that accepts both the aberrated image and a PSF map as inputs to generate a high-quality latent representation. By integrating lens-specific deep priors, this method offers a universal and adaptable solution for correcting optical aberrations. Specifically, we pre-train a base model using a diverse collection of lenses and then rapidly adapt it to specific lenses through parameter refinement, significantly reducing the time and memory required for model learning. The approach demonstrates high efficiency during both training and inference, with extensive results confirming its potential for use in compact, low-end camera systems.

Interactions between light probes and heavy bound states, such as black holes, generate observables rich in dynamical insights. Recently, a specific family of black hole microstates was demonstrated to possess an exact string worldsheet formulation. We have constructed the physical vertex operators for these models and determined their structure within the low-energy AdS$_3$ regime. Subsequently, we calculated a broad range of new heavy-light correlators in these settings. Notably, a portion of these results achieves the first correspondence between worldsheet correlators in black hole microstates and their holographically dual conformal field theory, representing a highly non-trivial agreement. Additionally, we propose a closed-form expression for heavy-light correlators involving any number of light insertions. As a practical application, we calculate the equivalent of the Hawking radiation rate for these microstates.

We introduce a batch trajectory optimizer capable of solving hundreds of distinct problem instances simultaneously in real-time. While designed for holonomic robots, our method relaxes the constraint requiring a circular base footprint. Our primary algorithmic advances are twofold: (i) enhancing the computational tractability of the inherent non-convex problem and (ii) utilizing batch processing to overcome initialization hurdles and elevate solution quality. These objectives are met by formulating kinematics and collision avoidance constraints as a multi-convex problem. By applying an Alternating Minimization strategy to exploit these structures, the resulting batch operation simplifies to matrix-vector products that are easily accelerated on GPUs. We advance the state-of-the-art in three key areas: first, we achieve superior navigation quality, including higher success rates and better tracking, compared to baseline methods that compute only a single locally optimal trajectory per control loop; second, when initialized with samples from a Gaussian distribution, our optimizer surpasses the current best cross-entropy method in terms of solution quality; and third, our approach is orders of magnitude faster than the conceptually simpler alternative of running parallel optimization instances on CPU threads. \textbf{Codes:} \url{https://tinyurl.com/a3b99m8}

Pulsed radio emissions from rotating neutron stars arise from slow resistive instabilities driven by an inhomogeneous twist profile within an open circuit. This study examines the stability of a weakly sheared, quantizing magnetic field where currents are sustained by a relativistic particle flow. In this environment, the electromagnetic field is nearly force-free, and particles remain in the lowest Landau state with negligible curvature drift. For a charge-neutral plasma, we identify multiple branches of slowly growing tearing modes—relativistic equivalents of the double tearing mode—with peak growth rates defined by $s \gtrsim 4\pi \widetilde k_y J_z/B_z$. Here, $B_z$ represents the strong, nearly potential guide field, $J_z$ is the field-aligned current density, and $\widetilde k_y$ is the mode wavenumber normalized to the current gradient scale. When the plasma possesses a net charge, these modes become overstable, exhibiting a real frequency $\omega \sim s\cdot |n_0^+ - n_0^-|/(n_0^+ + n_0^-)$ that scales with the imbalance between positive and negative charge densities. An isolated current sheet thinner than the skin depth sustains localized tearing modes whose growth rate scales as the inverse square root of the ratio of sheet thickness to skin depth. In a pulsar context, the peak growth rate approaches the angular rotation frequency ($s \gtrsim 2\widetilde k_y \Omega$), which is slow relative to longitudinal particle and field oscillations in a polar gap. These resistive modes display azimuthal drift similar to sub-pulse drift and represent a likely mechanism for pulse-to-pulse flux variations. Additionally, a companion paper investigates a Cerenkov-like instability of current-carrying Alfvén waves in thin current sheets with relativistic flows, proposing coherent curvature emission from these waves as a source of pulsar radio emission.

This study investigates the representation space of contextualized embeddings to uncover the hidden topology of large language models. We demonstrate the existence of a network of latent states that encapsulate linguistic properties within these representations. Rather than aligning with pre-existing annotations, we derive this latent network entirely unsupervised using a structured variational autoencoder. These induced states function as anchors that define the topology (neighborhoods and connectivity) of the representation manifold and expose the internal mechanisms of sentence encoding. Utilizing this network, we: (1) decompose the representation space into a spectrum of latent states capturing fine-grained word meanings through lexical, morphological, syntactic, and semantic dimensions; and (2) reveal that state-state transitions represent rich phrase constructions and form the backbone of the latent space. Combining these findings, we show that sentences are modeled as traversals across the latent network, where chains of state transitions encode syntactic templates and state-word emissions provide the specific content. We validate these insights through extensive experiments and visualizations.

This study addresses trajectory tracking control for an articulated unmanned ground vehicle by evaluating and comparing two distinct strategies regarding their performance and computational demands. The initial approach integrates a nonlinear model predictive controller (NMPC) with a nonlinear moving horizon estimator (NMHE), utilizing a nonlinear mathematical model derived from first principles. The alternative method employs input-state linearization (ISL) of the original model, followed by linear model predictive control (LMPC). We introduce a rapid real-time iteration scheme applied to the NMHE-NMPC framework and benchmark it against the conventional, cost-effective ISL-LMPC approach. Experimental data from time-based trajectories indicate that the NMHE-NMPC framework, enhanced with the proposed real-time iteration scheme, achieves superior trajectory tracking compared to the ISL-LMPC framework, with computation times suitable for real-time implementation. Furthermore, the ISL-LMPC method yields results of comparable quality to the NMHE-NMPC framework but at a significantly lower computational cost.

Although projection-based reduced order models lower the dimensionality of full-order solutions, the resulting reduced models may still include terms that scale with the full order size. Hyper-reduction techniques address this computational burden by using sampling-based approaches to approximate such terms with significantly smaller dimensions. This study introduces a points selection algorithm developed by Shin and Xiu [SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 38 (2016), pp. A385--A411] as a hyper-reduction method. Originally designed as a stochastic collocation technique for uncertainty quantification, the algorithm maximizes a metric $S$ that evaluates both column orthogonality and the determinant; consequently, it is designated as S-OPT. Numerical examples illustrate the algorithm's performance and compare it against an over-sampled Discrete Empirical Interpolation (DEIM) method. Results indicate that S-OPT predicts full-order solutions with greater accuracy for a specified number of indices.

Investigating Andreev bound states (ABSs) through transport is challenging due to the interaction between charging effects and superconductivity. This study contrasts transport-based ABS spectroscopy in a semiconductor-superconductor island with a charge-sensing method utilizing an integrated radio-frequency single-electron transistor. The agreement between these techniques confirms that rapid, non-invasive charge sensing enables precise quantitative analysis of ABSs while avoiding certain transport-related complications.

A systematic investigation of fully-heavy tetraquark states—specifically $cc\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $bb\bar{b}\bar{b}$, $bb\bar{c}\bar{c}$ (and its charge conjugate), $cb\bar{c}\bar{c}$, $cb\bar{b}\bar{b}$, and $cb\bar{c}\bar{b}$—is conducted using a non-relativistic quark model grounded in lattice-QCD findings regarding the two-body $Q\bar{Q}$ interaction. This interaction is modeled by a spin-independent Cornell potential supplemented with a spin-spin term. The four-body problem is addressed via the Gaussian expansion method, while the complex scaling technique is applied to uniformly treat bound, resonance, and scattering states. The study incorporates a comprehensive set of four-body configurations, including meson-meson, diquark-antidiquark, and K-type arrangements, along with their couplings, for spin-parity quantum numbers $J^{P(C)}=0^{+(+)}$, $1^{+(\pm)}$, and $2^{+(+)}$ within the $S$-wave channel. Results reveal several narrow resonances across all examined systems, characterized by two-meson strong decay widths below 30 MeV. Notably, the fully-charm resonances recently observed by the LHCb Collaboration in the di-$J/\psi$ invariant spectrum (between 6.2 and 7.2 GeV) are successfully reproduced. In the fully-bottom sector, resonances are predicted with masses ranging from 18.9 to 19.6 GeV, while the remaining charm-bottom configurations yield masses between 9.8 and 16.4 GeV. These predicted states offer targets for verification in future experimental efforts.

A digraph $G$ is defined as \emph{$k$-geodetic} if, for every pair of vertices $u,v \in V(G)$, there exists at most one walk of length $\leq k$ connecting $u$ to $v$. This paper establishes the maximum possible order of a $k$-geodetic digraph. Furthermore, it addresses the more challenging question of the largest size of a strongly-connected $k$-geodetic digraph, providing a solution for $k = 2$ and presenting a construction believed to be optimal for larger values of $k$. The study concludes with findings regarding generalized Tur\'{a}n problems concerning the counts of directed cycles and paths within $k$-geodetic digraphs.

This paper examines the classical singular integral operator defined on a local field with rough kernels, analyzing its boundedness across various function spaces by loosening the requirements for kernel smoothness.

We analyze a fully-coupled system of McKean-Vlasov stochastic differential equations with slow and fast components, where both the components and the law of the slow variable exert full influence, and we establish convergence rates toward the homogenized limit. While we avoid assuming periodicity, we impose specific conditions on the fast dynamics to ensure ergodicity. The proof process yields related ergodic theorems and provides insights into the regularity of Poisson-type equations and their associated Cauchy problems on the Wasserstein space, findings that hold independent significance.

By utilizing the functional renormalization group method at next-to-leading order within the derivative expansion, we have improved upon our previous results regarding the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity in classic O(N) universality classes. For the QCD-relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma} = 1.607(2)$ and $1.589(2)$ for $N=2$ and $N=4$, respectively. Additionally, we derived $|z_c| = 2.03(8)$ and $1.68(3)$ for $N=2$ and $N=4$, though these values carry larger systematic uncertainties.

Photon losses are an inherent characteristic of any translationally invariant optical imaging system possessing a non-trivial Point Spread Function, and the connection between transmission factors and the coherence of imaged objects is universal—a claim we rigorously prove using quantum mechanical principles. We subsequently derive the fundamental limit on estimating the separation between two partially coherent sources. By meticulously examining the impact of photon losses, we resolve conflicting assertions found in prior research. Calculating the Quantum Fisher Information for a generic optical 4f imaging system, we utilize preliminary considerations to confirm these results for any general, translationally invariant imaging device. We demonstrate that the spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) measurement, which is optimal for non-coherent sources, retains its optimality across any degree of coherence. Furthermore, we reveal that approximations commonly found in theoretical optical imaging literature inevitably produce unphysical models with zero transmission, leading to erroneous conclusions about fundamental resolution limits.

Numerical simulations play a pivotal role in forecasting the space debris landscape for the coming decades. As debris-generating activities, such as ongoing anti-satellite tests and the deployment of mega-constellations, intensify, precise predictions become essential for maintaining the long-term viability of critical satellite orbits. Due to the computational demands of accurately propagating long-term trajectories for vast numbers of objects, numerical models typically depend on Monte-Carlo methods for stochastic conjunction analysis. Conversely, deterministic methods offer superior accuracy and are valuable for validating stochastic models, yet they present significant challenges regarding computational feasibility. This study introduces the architecture and proof-of-concept results for a deterministic conjunction tracking simulation capable of modeling debris evolution over decades. To achieve this, we developed a high-performance propagator in modern C++ that accounts for Earth's gravitational anomalies, solar radiation pressure, and atmospheric drag, utilizing AutoPAS—a sophisticated particle container that automatically optimizes data structures and algorithms. We present findings from a 20-year simulation of 16,024 particles in low-Earth orbit, where conjunctions were tracked to identify and analyze both predicted collisions and close encounters. A detailed examination of the simulation's runtime and computational costs reveals that modern computing tools now make deterministic conjunction tracking feasible. These results demonstrate the ability to validate previous findings and construct higher-fidelity simulations of the long-term space debris environment.

In contemporary statistics and machine learning, a key objective is often demonstrating that first-order methods applied to non-convex risk functions eventually converge to a parameter region where the risk becomes locally convex. We introduce an asymptotic comparison inequality termed the Sudakov-Fernique post-AMP inequality; within a specific class of problems involving GOE matrices, this tool allows for the analysis of optimization landscape properties near the iterates of an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. To illustrate its utility, we present a novel and potentially more straightforward proof of certain findings by Celentano et al. (2021), which show that the TAP free energy in the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-synchronization problem is locally convex within the region to which AMP converges. Additionally, we confirm a conjecture by El Alaoui et al. (2022) regarding the local convexity of a related yet distinct TAP free energy. This result implies that their algorithm efficiently samples from the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Gibbs measure across the "easy" regime.

This work examines the dynamics of a rigid rotator on the SU(2) group manifold as a specific case of motion on Lie groups, alongside a dual model defined on the Borel group SB(2,C), which serves as the Lie Poisson dual of SU(2). We propose a parent action formulated on the Drinfel'd double of these groups, representing a system with double the degrees of freedom of the original pair. By applying a gauging procedure to the global symmetries of this parent action, both the rigid rotor and the dual model are successfully reconstructed.

Quantum tasks are defined as quantum computations where inputs and outputs are localized at specific spacetime points. Analyzing these tasks within the AdS/CFT framework has yielded new connections between boundary entanglement and bulk geometry. This paper extends the study to scenarios where inputs and outputs are encoded in extended spacetime regions instead of single points. We demonstrate that this extension imposes stricter constraints than those derived from point-based analyses. Specifically, we enhance the connected wedge theorem (originally presented in 1912.05649) by identifying a more extensive bulk region whose presence necessitates significant boundary correlations. Furthermore, we illustrate how incorporating extended input and output regions generates non-trivial results in Poincaré-AdS$_{2+1}$, a context in which the point-based version of the connected wedge theorem yields only trivial outcomes.

We introduce a min-max framework for specific complete minimal hypersurfaces within hyperbolic space. Specifically, we demonstrate that for any two strictly stable minimal hypersurfaces sharing the same ideal boundary at infinity, a new hypersurface exists that lies between them. As a consequence, we prove that under a low entropy constraint, all minimal hypersurfaces asymptotic to a common ideal boundary are isotopic.

The edge density and temperature of tokamak plasmas are tightly linked to energy and particle confinement, making their quantification essential for grasping edge dynamics. These parameters display behaviors spanning from sharp gradients and rapid transient events (such as shifts between low and high confinement regimes) to steady stationary states. Consequently, analyzing experimental edge data demands robust fitting methods capable of capturing complex spatiotemporal evolution. Furthermore, since fusion plasma diagnostics inherently contain measurement errors, a statistical framework is necessary to precisely quantify uncertainties. This paper presents a generalized, multidimensional adaptive Gaussian process routine designed to automatically manage noisy data and spatiotemporal correlations. We concentrate on the edge-pedestal region to highlight progress in characterizing time-dependent plasma profiles, specifically regarding transport barrier formation on the Alcator C-Mod tokamak.

Knowledge distillation (KD) has garnered significant attention in deep learning as a powerful and efficient approach for model compression, primarily by transferring knowledge from a large teacher network to a smaller student one. However, most current KD methods rely on a single distillation strategy that captures only one type of knowledge—either instance features or instance relations. There is a scarcity of research exploring a unified framework that transfers multiple knowledge types using distinct distillation strategies. Furthermore, traditional offline distillation often faces limited learning capacity because of fixed teacher-student architectures. To address these issues, this paper introduces Collaborative Teacher-Student Learning via Multiple Knowledge Transfer (CTSL-MKT), which facilitates both self-learning and collaborative learning. This approach enables multiple students to learn from both individual instances and their relational structures collaboratively. While engaging in self-distillation, these students also guide one another through online distillation. Experimental results and ablation studies across four image datasets demonstrate that the proposed CTSL-MKT significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art KD methods.

This study introduces a wideband subspace estimation technique that defines the signal subspace via its orthogonal projection matrix at every frequency. The core approach models this matrix as a frequency-dependent function, which is approximated using a polynomial. This method offers two key benefits: it reduces the number of parameters needed to represent the signal subspace across a frequency band and enhances the performance of wideband direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimators, specifically Incoherent Multiple Signal Classification (IC-MUSIC) and Modified Test of Orthogonality of Projected Subspaces (MTOPS). Essentially, the technique fits a polynomial to projection matrix estimates derived from various frequencies and employs this polynomial as the subspace representation. Furthermore, the paper derives asymptotic bounds for the bias and root-mean-square (RMS) error of the projection matrix estimate and provides a numerical evaluation of the proposed method alongside its integration with the aforementioned DOA estimators.

Accurate segmentation of brain tumors is crucial for diagnosing and prognosing glioma patients. The ongoing brain tumor segmentation challenge offers a valuable dataset for developing automatic segmentation algorithms. This paper outlines our contribution to the 2021 competition, building upon nn-UNet, the winning model from the previous year. We explored various modifications, such as increasing network size, substituting batch normalization with group normalization, and integrating axial attention into the decoder. Both internal 5-fold cross-validation and online evaluations by the organizers confirmed the efficacy of our approach, yielding slight quantitative improvements over the baseline. Ultimately, our models secured first place in the final ranking on unseen test data. The source code, pretrained weights, and Docker image for the winning submission are publicly accessible at https://github.com/rixez/Brats21_KAIST_MRI_Lab.

Multi-band transmission systems have arisen as a viable solution to the capacity constraints of silica-based optical fibers by leveraging the fiber's entire low-loss spectrum. Furthermore, elastic optical networks (EON) were introduced to optimize the management of scarce resources within optical networks. The core challenge in operating an EON involves selecting the appropriate route, modulation format, and spectrum allocation. To address this, it is crucial to understand the accumulation of linear and nonlinear impairments as signals propagate through an optical fiber link. This study establishes the maximum propagation distance for optical signals in a multi-band environment, evaluating various modulation formats against commonly used thresholds in EON.

We present the deployment and initial observations of CONCERTO, a large field-of-view (18.6 arc-min) spectral imaging instrument. Mounted on the 12-meter APEX telescope at 5100 meters above sea level on the Chajnantor plateau, the instrument functions within the 130–310 GHz range. It utilizes a rapid (2.5 Hz mechanical frequency) Fourier Transform Spectrometer (FTS) paired with a continuous dilution cryostat achieving a base temperature of 60 mK to produce spectra with a resolution of R=1–300. The cryostat houses the cold optics and front-end electronics alongside two 2152-pixel Lumped Element Kinetic Inductance Detector (LEKID) arrays. After installation in April 2021, CONCERTO generates over 20,000 spectra per second. This paper details the instrument's final development stages, installation process, and early results from sky observations.

Deploying deep learning on edge devices relies heavily on model compression, where quantizing weights and activations into low-precision formats reduces memory usage and inference latency. However, accurately predicting how a model responds to these changes remains difficult due to the non-linear and heterogeneous nature of the impact across the network. Identifying which specific parameters and activations are most sensitive to quantization is essential for optimizing efficiency. To address this, we introduce FIT, a method grounded in information geometry that integrates Fisher information with a quantization model. FIT can forecast a network's final performance without the need for retraining by merging the effects of both parameter and activation quantization into one unified metric. Compared to current approaches, FIT is computationally efficient and exhibits strong convergence characteristics. These advantages are empirically validated across hundreds of quantization setups, with particular emphasis on layer-wise mixed-precision strategies.

Satellite communication systems are experiencing a resurgence in both academic and industrial sectors, driven by innovative offerings from major technology firms and their potential to support global connectivity goals within early 6G frameworks. On one side, advancements in manufacturing and radio technologies promise to lower service costs while ensuring superior latency, bandwidth, flexibility, and coverage. Conversely, cybersecurity measures for SATCOM links must evolve to address the significantly enhanced capabilities of attackers over the past twenty years. Despite this, business urgency and opportunities are pushing operators toward difficult system compromises, inadvertently expanding the attack surface and diluting available security protections. This paper addresses these issues by providing a comprehensive survey of link-layer security threats, solutions, and challenges inherent to deploying and operating SATCOM systems. Specifically, the literature on SATCOM security is categorized into two primary areas: physical-layer security and cryptographic schemes. Within these branches, specific research domains are identified, focusing on dedicated security concerns such as physical-layer confidentiality, anti-jamming, anti-spoofing, and quantum-based key distribution. For each domain, key techniques, unique characteristics, pros and cons, practical lessons, and future trajectories are highlighted. Finally, the paper outlines emerging research topics that, if further explored by academia and industry, could attract additional researchers and investors, thereby unlocking the full potential of ubiquitous satellite communications.

This study reports the inaugural measurement of the cross section for Cabibbo-suppressed $\Lambda$ baryon production, utilizing data from the MicroBooNE detector exposed to neutrinos from the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory's Main Injector beam. The analysis encompasses $2.2 \times 10^{20}$ protons on target during neutrino mode and $4.9 \times 10^{20}$ protons on target during anti-neutrino mode. An automated selection process, supplemented by manual scanning, identified five candidate $\Lambda$ production events upon unblinding, which aligns with the GENIE prediction of $5.3 \pm 0.8$ events. Multiple scanners yielded between three and five events, compared against a blinded Monte Carlo simulation forecast of $3.7 \pm 1.0$ events. By restricting the phase space to $\Lambda$ baryons decaying above MicroBooNE's detection thresholds, we derive a flux-averaged cross section of $2.0^{+2.1}_{-1.6} \times 10^{-40}$ cm$^2$/Ar, with combined statistical and systematic uncertainties.

We provide a proof demonstrating that in any weakly coupled quantum field theory possessing a finite global symmetry group $\mathrm{G}$ on a compact spatial manifold, the density of states $\rho_\alpha(E)$ for every irreducible representation $\alpha$ of $\mathrm{G}$ follows a universal formula at sufficiently high energies, as conjectured by Harlow and Ooguri. This result extends analogous findings from $(1+1)$ dimensions to higher spacetime dimensions. The proof hinges on the approximate existence of a Hilbert series within the weakly coupled regime and is also relevant for computing twisted supersymmetric indices. Additionally, we examine the case of continuous $\mathrm{G}$, proving a distinct yet universal behavior, and discuss the significance of averaging in the density of states.

Identifying abnormal areas within urban datasets represents a critical research challenge. To the best of our knowledge, existing approaches for spatio-temporal anomalies rely on road or grid structures, which often lead to data sparsity and degrade detection performance. To overcome these limitations, this paper introduces a dynamic region partitioning technique. Additionally, we present an unsupervised framework for REgional Anomaly Detection (ReAD) capable of identifying irregularly shaped abnormal zones by jointly leveraging spatial and temporal characteristics. Specifically, the framework initially generates regions using the dynamic partitioning method, ensuring that observations within each region share adjacent locations and similar non-spatial attributes; this strategy mitigates data sparsity and heterogeneity more effectively than grid-based methods. Subsequently, an anomaly metric is computed for each region through a regional divergence calculation. Finally, abnormal regions are identified using either a weighted or a wavy approach, depending on the specific scenario. Experiments conducted on both simulated datasets and real-world applications validate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed framework.

Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) ferromagnets, particularly the recently discovered CrI$_3$ and Cr$_2$Ge$_2$Te$_6$, have revitalized interest in 2D magnetism due to their potential in spintronics. This study presents a systematic investigation of the 2H-Mn$_{0.28}$TaS$_2$ single crystal, a 2D vdW ferromagnet characterized by a Curie temperature ($T_c$) of approximately 82.3 K and significant in-plane magnetic anisotropy. Mn $K$-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy was employed to characterize its electronic state and local atomic structure. Magnetic isotherms measured near $T_c$ reveal that spin coupling within 2H-Mn$_{0.28}$TaS$_2$ follows a three-dimensional (3D) Heisenberg model, coupled with attractive long-range interactions decaying as $J(r)\approx r^{-4.85}$. Anomalies in both resistivity $\rho(T)$ and thermopower $S(T)$ near $T_c$ confirm strong interactions between hole-type charge carriers and local magnetic moments. Additionally, an anomalous angle-dependent magnetoresistance was detected, hinting at a potential field-induced novel magnetic configuration.

This study presents measurements of top quark polarization and spin correlations in top quark pairs ($\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$) derived from events featuring two oppositely charged leptons ($e^+e^-$, $e^\pm\mu^\mp$, or $\mu^+\mu^-$) generated in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. Recorded by the CMS experiment at the LHC in 2016, the dataset corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 fb$^{-1}$. For the first time at this energy, a set of parton-level normalized differential cross sections was measured to probe the independent coefficients of the spin-dependent components of the $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ production density matrix. These measured distributions and extracted coefficients were compared against standard model predictions from next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD simulations and NLO QCD calculations incorporating electroweak corrections. All results align with standard model expectations. Furthermore, fits utilizing the normalized differential cross sections constrain the anomalous chromomagnetic and chromoelectric dipole moments of the top quark to the ranges $-0.24 < C_\text{tG}/\Lambda^{2} < 0.07$ TeV$^{-2}$ and $-0.33 < C^{I}_\text{tG}/\Lambda^{2} < 0.20$ TeV$^{-2}$, respectively, at a 95% confidence level.

This study examines quantum dots within semiconductor PbTe nanowire devices. Because ambipolar transport is accessible in PbTe, these quantum dots can be populated by either electrons or holes. Given PbTe's exceptionally high dielectric constant, approximately 1000, the usual Coulomb blockade that often obscures orbital and spin spectra is absent. Consequently, we have determined large, highly anisotropic effective Lande g-factors ranging from 20 to 44. The lack of Coulomb blockade enables the direct measurement, even at zero source-drain bias, of spin-orbit hybridization energies reaching up to 600 microelectronvolts. These distinctive spin characteristics position recently synthesized PbTe nanowires—a member of the group IV-VI materials family—as a promising platform for quantum technologies, including the development of spin and topological qubits.

For an $n \times n$ involutory matrix $A$, singular values $\sigma > 1$ occur in reciprocal pairs $(\sigma, 1/\sigma)$, whereas $\sigma = 1$ can appear either singly or as the pair $(1, 1)$. The left and right singular vectors associated with these paired values are intrinsically linked. By leveraging this relationship, the singular value decomposition (SVD) of an involutory matrix can be reformulated as an eigendecomposition, revealing a notable connection between its singular values and eigenvalues. Comparable insights apply to the SVD, singular values, and coneigenvalues of (skew-)coninvolutory matrices.

The accessibility of 3D printers across various sizes and price points has made them available beyond professional users. Nevertheless, achieving perfect operation remains difficult, particularly with the Fused Deposition Method, where accurate calibration poses significant challenges. While prior research indicated that machine learning could identify these issues using sensor and image data, practical implementation was hindered by the need for additional sensor installations. Focusing on future real-world application, this study aims to develop a lightweight early detection model using easily collectible data. The proposed Convolutional Neural Network model demonstrates high fault classification accuracy, achieving 96.72% for binary classification and 93.38% for multi-classification. Ultimately, this research seeks to enable general users to operate 3D printers with greater accuracy.

Understanding the thermodynamic behavior of non-equilibrium polymer chains is a core challenge in both polymer and biological physics. Through molecular dynamics simulations, we identified a universal non-equilibrium mechanism governing polar active polymers: head activity dictates the entire chain's behavior, leading to re-entrant swelling and a non-monotonic change in the Flory exponent $\nu$. These unique phenomena stem from a head-controlled railway motion, which generates two opposing non-equilibrium effects—dynamic chain rigidity and chain conformation involution marked by negative bond vector correlation. The interplay between these effects dictates the polymer's configuration. Furthermore, we characterized several generic dynamic traits of polar active polymers, including a linear decay in the end-to-end vector correlation function, a size-dependent crossover from ballistic to diffusive motion, and a diffusion coefficient independent of polymer length but sensitive to head activity. We propose a straightforward dynamic theory that accurately accounts for these dynamic observations. This pronounced structural and dynamical responsiveness of active polymers to head activity offers a practical method for controlling active agents, with significant implications for biomedical engineering.

We demonstrate a general alternative circular summation formula for theta functions, which yields numerous theta-function identities. Specifically, this result allows us to recover several identities found in Ramanujan's Notebook. Additionally, we derive two distinct formulas for $(q;q)_\infty^{2n}$.

While Landauer's principle dictates a minimum energy cost for erasing a single bit, Vaccaro and Barnett (VB) recently showed that within generalized Gibbs ensembles, erasing information from energy-degenerate spin reservoirs can be achieved solely through a minimum expenditure of spin angular momentum, bypassing energy costs. Unlike the standard Landauer scenario, this VB cost depends on a discrete variable. This study investigates the discrete fluctuations associated with this cost and the likelihood of violating the VB bound, deriving a Jarzynski-like equality for the protocol. We discover that fluctuations falling below the VB bound are suppressed exponentially at a significantly faster and tighter rate than those in an equivalent Jarzynski expression. Furthermore, we reveal a trade-off between fluctuation magnitude and erasure cost, noting that the discrete nature of these fluctuations becomes prominent when reservoir spins are maximally polarized. Additionally, we formulate the first laws of thermodynamics governing spin angular momentum conservation for this specific erasure method. These findings are crucial for developing novel heat engines utilizing information erasure schemes that avoid energy expenditure.

It is a well-established fact that inverse problems are ill-posed, necessitating the use of regularization methods to derive meaningful solutions. Historically, penalized variational approaches have been the standard for such tasks. However, in recent years, deep-learning-based learned reconstruction algorithms have surpassed these classical methods in performance. Despite their empirical success, these learned algorithms lack the robust theoretical foundations—specifically regarding stability and regularization—that characterize traditional approaches. Consequently, their outputs cannot always be fully trusted, as they may exhibit instabilities or generate hallucinated features inherent to the learning process. Research indicates that these algorithms are highly vulnerable to minor adversarial noise in the data, which can cause severe instabilities in the recovered solution distinct from those of the underlying ill-posed problem. In contrast, classical regularization methods are capable of effectively managing such adversarial noise to ensure stable recovery. This work proposes specific regularization strategies to stabilize these otherwise unstable learned reconstruction techniques, enabling the recovery of regularized solutions even under adversarial conditions. To achieve this, we extend the classical concept of regularization and integrate it into learned algorithms. Furthermore, we introduce regularization techniques tailored for two prominent learned reconstruction frameworks: Learned Post-Processing Reconstruction and Learned Unrolling Reconstruction.

Covert channels are stealthy and unpredictable communication pathways that facilitate various adversarial activities, such as the secret exfiltration of sensitive data or the covert management of botnets. Conversely, they can also serve legitimate purposes, like enabling journalists to exchange confidential information. Consequently, all covert channels discussed thus far must disguise their data transfer by mimicking seemingly benign information flows and unsuspicious behavior.

This paper introduces DYST (Did You See That?), a novel category of covert channels termed "history covert channels." These channels rely almost entirely on unmodified, legitimate traffic generated by standard network participants, requiring only a negligible amount of actual covert data transfer. We expand the existing covert channel taxonomy to categorize history channels, provide a theoretical analysis of their characteristics, and demonstrate how to optimize their configuration for two specific implementations: DYST-Basic and DYST-Ext. Additionally, we present proof-of-concept code for both variants and evaluate their performance regarding robustness, detectability, and optimization using both simulated and real-world traffic. Finally, we examine potential application scenarios and discuss countermeasures against DYST.

This study addresses how to effectively guide content selection in Transformer-based abstractive summarization by introducing a simple yet powerful attention head masking technique applied to encoder-decoder attentions during inference to identify salient content. This approach elucidates the connection between encoder-decoder attention patterns and the models' content selection mechanisms. Evaluated across three document summarization datasets in both in-domain and cross-domain scenarios, our method demonstrates superior performance compared to prior state-of-the-art models on the CNN/Daily Mail and New York Times datasets. Furthermore, the inference-time masking strategy exhibits high data efficiency, achieving better results than BART fine-tuned on the complete CNN/DailyMail dataset using only 20% of the training samples.

The non-resonant mechanism's dependence of nucleon polarization on various invariant variables within the reaction $e^+ + e^- \to N + \bar{N} +\pi^0$ has been established. This polarization is formulated using six invariant complex amplitudes, based on the conservation of hadron electromagnetic currents and the P-invariance of the hadron electromagnetic interaction. The study considers an inclusive experimental configuration where protons (or antiprotons) and pions are detected in coincidence. Numerical evaluations for the normal polarization were conducted across the energy range from threshold to $s=16$ GeV$^2$, employing a specific parametrization of nucleon electromagnetic form factors and incorporating the previously calculated unpolarized differential cross section of the non-resonant mechanism.

Let $V$ be a smooth quasi-projective complex surface characterized by three initial logarithmic plurigenera equal to 1 and a logarithmic irregularity of 2. We demonstrate that the quasi-Albanese morphism of $V$ is birational and that there exists a finite set $S$ such that the quasi-Albanese map is proper over the complement of $S$ within the quasi-Albanese variety $A(V)$. This result provides a sharp, effective refinement of a classical theorem by Iitaka.

Compressed bitmap indexes, such as Roaring, are employed by systems like Git and Oracle to speed up query performance. These structures represent sets and facilitate operations including unions, intersections, differences, and symmetric differences. Major platforms including Elasticsearch, Apache Spark, Netflix's Atlas, LinkedIn's Pinot, Metamarkets' Druid, Pilosa, Apache Hive, Apache Tez, Microsoft Visual Studio Team Services, and Apache Kylin depend on the Roaring format. We introduce CRoaring, an optimized C library implementing Roaring bitmaps that leverages Single-Instruction-Multiple-Data (SIMD) instructions common on commodity processors. Specifically, we detail vectorized algorithms for calculating intersections, unions, differences, and symmetric differences across arrays. Through extensive benchmarking against various competitors, we analyze the strengths and weaknesses of our software. This work is released under a permissive open-source license.

Explaining the universe's baryon asymmetry necessitates new sources of CP violation beyond those provided by the Standard Model (SM). Measuring a non-zero permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) in fundamental particles—such as electrons or neutrons—or in nuclei and atoms offers a crucial pathway to identifying these CP-violating origins, both within and outside the SM. The SM itself contains multiple mechanisms for generating CP-violating EDMs, specifically through the CKM matrix in the weak sector and the QCD $ ar{	heta}$ parameter in the strong sector. This work estimates the maximum possible EDMs for various leptons ($e^-$, $\mu^-$, $	au^-$, $
u_e^0$, $
u^0_{\mu}$, $
u^0_{	au}$), baryons ($n^0$, $p^+$, $\Lambda^0$, $\Sigma^0$, $\Xi^0$, $\Lambda^+_c$, $\Xi^+_c$), atoms ($^{85}$Rb, $^{133}$Cs, $^{210}$Fr, $^{205}$Tl, $^{199}$Hg, $^{129}$Xe, $^{225}$Ra, $^{223}$Rn), and molecules (HfF$^+$, PbO, YbF, ThO, RaF, TlF) within the (CKM$ igoplus ar{	heta}$) framework, assuming each EDM arises exclusively from either the CKM or $ ar{	heta}$ mechanism independently. These theoretical limits are evaluated against current experimental upper bounds. Crucially, the study demonstrates that constraints on CP-violating parameters vary across different systems; thus, identical EDM measurement limits in two distinct systems do not necessarily impose equal constraints on CP-violating parameters. Consequently, measuring non-zero EDMs across multiple systems remains essential for fully understanding the origins of CP-violating EDMs.

This paper introduces a deep structured tracking framework designed for a large cohort of decision-makers. The problem is modeled as a linear quadratic deep structured team, wherein agents cooperatively pursue a global objective while simultaneously attending to local targets. In unconstrained scenarios, the gauge transformation technique decomposes the optimization task, yielding a low-dimensional optimal control strategy expressed through local and global Riccati equations. However, for constrained scenarios, the gauge transformation does not guarantee a decomposable feasible set. To address this, we propose a suite of local and global receding horizon control problems; a specific linear combination of their solutions generates a feasible outcome for the original constrained problem. A key advantage of these solutions is their scalability with respect to the number of decision-makers and their suitability for distributed implementation. Moreover, the primary findings are extended to accommodate multiple sub-populations and diverse features, such as leader-follower configurations, cohesive cost functions, and soft structural constraints. Additionally, the study defines a class of cyber-physical attacks via perturbed influence factors and includes a numerical example to validate the proposed results.

This study examines how spin-orbit coupling influences proximity-induced superconductivity in a normal metal connected to a superconductor. Specifically, we analyze a heterostructure where interfaces generate Rashba spin-orbit coupling, exploring the resulting superconducting properties using the tunneling Hamiltonian formalism. Our findings indicate that spin-orbit coupling creates a mixture of singlet and triplet pairing states; under certain conditions, this leads to the emergence of odd-frequency, even-parity, spin-triplet pairs. Furthermore, we evaluate the impact of impurity scattering on these induced pairs and contextualize our results within heterostructures featuring materials that exhibit spin-momentum locking.

This study examines Solomon's zeta function for orders within a specific context: those generated by the standard basis of an integral table algebra, which includes the integral adjacency algebra of an association scheme as a subset. Since Solomon's original elementary technique encounters computational challenges when dealing with ranks of 3 or higher, a more efficient approach is necessary. We present multiple examples demonstrating how to utilize the local zeta integral method introduced by Bushnell and Reiner to calculate explicit zeta functions for these orders.

Many resource allocation scenarios involve diverse resource types, where distinct agencies manage the local distribution of each type, yet a central planner aims to ensure the final allocation meets specific criteria based on agents' preferences. This paper examines the link between the characteristics of these individual local mechanisms—each tasked with assigning a specific resource type—and those of a sequential mechanism formed by applying these local mechanisms one after another, specifically under lexicographic preferences, a widely recognized preference model in economics and AI. We demonstrate that when preferences are O-legal (indicating agents share a common priority order for resource types), a sequential mechanism satisfies desirable attributes such as anonymity, neutrality, non-bossiness, or Pareto-optimality if and only if every constituent local mechanism also possesses that property, provided they are applied in the sequence dictated by order O. Our primary findings establish that, under O-legal lexicographic preferences, any mechanism that is strategyproof and satisfies a specific combination of these properties must essentially be a sequential composition of local mechanisms that are themselves strategyproof and adhere to the same property combinations.

Accurately compensating for brain shift through a robust ultrasound-to-ultrasound registration technique would significantly enhance Image-Guided Neurological Surgery. However, developing such a method is difficult due to challenges including sparse feature correspondence, complex pathological anatomy, and the need for rapid computation. To address this, we introduce a novel active framework driven by features. The process begins by estimating landmarks and their displacements from a pair of ultrasound images via local feature matching. A Gaussian Process (GP) model then interpolates a dense deformation field from these sparse landmarks, with kernels derived using variograms and a discrete grid search. Furthermore, the system allows users to actively introduce additional landmarks based on visual context and the GP's uncertainty metrics to refine the outcome. We retrospectively validate this registration framework as a reliable and precise solution for brain shift compensation using clinical data from neurosurgical procedures.

Local windows are standard in computer vision, typically centered on the pixel under processing. However, we demonstrate that this convention is not universally beneficial; specifically, centering the window on a pixel located at an edge is a primary cause of blurring in many filtering algorithms. Leveraging this insight, we introduce Side Window Filtering (SWF), a method that aligns the window's side or corner with the target pixel instead. Despite its simplicity and strong theoretical foundation, SWF proves highly effective. We illustrate that numerous traditional linear and nonlinear filters can be readily adapted to the SWF framework. Comprehensive analysis and experiments indicate that adopting the SWF principle significantly enhances edge preservation, yielding state-of-the-art results in tasks such as image smoothing, denoising, enhancement, texture removal while preserving structure, mutual-structure extraction, and HDR tone mapping. Beyond filtering, we show that SWF extends to other local-window applications; for instance, in colorization via optimization, it effectively mitigates artifacts like color leakage common in conventional approaches. Given the prevalence of window-based operations in computer vision, the SWF technique holds potential to benefit a wide range of applications.

A generalized numerical semigroup is defined as a submonoid of $\mathbb{N}^d$ possessing a finite complement. This study investigates three distinct classes of such semigroups. Specifically, we demonstrate that the first class fulfills a generalized version of Wilf's conjecture by extending a well-known sufficient condition for Wilf's conjecture in numerical semigroups, which incorporates the semigroup's type. Furthermore, we derive partial results regarding Wilf's generalized conjecture for the remaining two classes and outline several open questions.
We demonstrate that any valuation ring which includes its residue field of characteristic $p>0$ can be expressed as a filtered direct limit of complete intersection ${\bf F}_p$-algebras.

We introduce a comprehensive framework for describing drag forces on a condensate resulting from interactions with a moving thermal bath of non-condensate particles, building upon prior theories regarding condensate equilibration within a trap. This model effectively simulates the previously observed polariton drag phenomenon, where an electric current flowing through a polariton condensate induces measurable momentum transfer and an effective potential energy shift.

We present a room-temperature sideband-resolved cavity electromechanical system. In this setup, a dielectrically coupled three-dimensional copper microwave cavity interacts with a strongly pre-stressed silicon nitride string. The electromechanical coupling is verified through two distinct measurements: the cavity-induced shift in the mechanical resonator's eigenfrequency, which is primarily driven by dielectric effects, and optomechanically induced transparency, which distinctly demonstrates the dynamical backaction of the cavity field on the resonator. These findings open the door for room-temperature applications in cavity electromechanics.

Evolutionary Game Theory (EGT) simulations model populations undergoing biological and cultural evolution across diverse disciplines, including biology, economics, and linguistics. This paper introduces DyPy, an open-source Python library capable of executing evolutionary simulations for any matrix-form game using three standard dynamics: Moran, Wright-Fisher, and Replicator. We outline the package's core components and demonstrate its application in running various simulations. DyPy enables users to conduct these simulations with minimal effort and little prior Python experience. We anticipate that this tool will serve as a valuable resource for researchers across multiple fields.

This study investigates the nonlinear response of a dimer consisting of two identical Mie-resonant dielectric nanoparticles when illuminated normally with circularly polarized light. We formulate a general theory outlining the hybridization of multipolar modes within these coupled nanoparticles and demonstrate a non-zero nonlinear circular dichroism (CD) in the second-harmonic generation (SHG) signal. This effect is amplified by multipolar resonances, provided the dimer's axis is tilted relative to the dielectric material's crystalline lattice. Furthermore, we present experimental data on this SHG-CD phenomenon using AlGaAs dimers situated on an engineered substrate, which validate the fundamental predictions of our multipolar hybridization framework.

This study systematically examines how the presence of extreme outliers affects both active and passive (index) investment strategies. We demonstrate that active managers encounter substantial risks of underperformance primarily because they often fail to capture these major winners. To investigate this phenomenon, we utilize both numerical simulations and analytical methods.

This paper investigates the boundedness of a broad class of multi-sublinear operators $T_m$, along with their commutators $T^{b}_{m,i}$ ($i=1,\cdots,m$), which are derived from multilinear Calder{\'o}n-Zygmund operators. The analysis focuses on these operators acting within the framework of product generalized mixed Morrey spaces $M^{\varphi_1}_{\vec{q_1}}({\Bbb R}^n)\times\cdots\times M^{\varphi_m}_{\vec{q_m}}({\Bbb R}^n)$. We establish sufficient conditions on the parameters $(\varphi_1,\cdots,\varphi_m,\varphi)$ that guarantee the boundedness of $T_m$ from the product space to $M^{\varphi}_{\vec{q}}({\Bbb R}^n)$. Furthermore, we examine the corresponding sufficient conditions for the boundedness of the commutators $T^b_{m,i}$ between the same spaces. As applications of these results, we derive boundedness properties for the multi-sublinear maximal operator, the multilinear Calder{\'o}n-Zygmund operator, and their commutators on product generalized mixed Morrey spaces.

The global proliferation of cloud data centers (CDCs) has created a pervasive need for hosting application services, while modern data-intensive sectors have significantly increased the resource demands of contemporary applications. Consequently, the deployment of a larger number of cloud servers has escalated energy consumption, raising critical sustainability issues. Traditional approaches, including heuristic and reinforcement learning algorithms, only partially address scalability and adaptability challenges. Moreover, existing solutions frequently overlook the interdependencies between host thermal profiles, task resource usage, and scheduling choices, resulting in suboptimal scalability and elevated compute requirements, especially under non-stationary demand conditions. To overcome these shortcomings, we introduce HUNTER, an AI-driven holistic resource management framework designed for sustainable cloud computing. This model frames energy optimization as a multi-objective scheduling problem that integrates energy, thermal, and cooling models. HUNTER employs a Gated Graph Convolution Network as a surrogate model to estimate Quality of Service (QoS) for specific system states and derive optimal scheduling strategies. Evaluations conducted in both simulated and physical cloud environments using CloudSim and the COSCO framework demonstrate that HUNTER surpasses state-of-the-art baselines by up to 12%, 35%, 43%, 54%, and 3% in energy consumption, SLA violations, scheduling time, cost, and temperature, respectively.

Recent experimental and theoretical studies of neural populations in two distinct early sensory systems, olfaction and vision, have contested the idea that they function under different computational frameworks. This challenge is supported by evidence showing that their respective population codes share three core characteristics: high redundancy, organization where information is conveyed by the identity of active neurons rather than their relative timing, and the capacity for error correction. We introduce the first general model that encapsulates these three traits, enabling an investigation into whether similar structures exist in other population codes. Furthermore, our model offers specific predictions regarding additional, previously unobserved structural elements within these codes. If empirical data confirms these predictions, it would offer new support for the hypothesis that such population codes adhere to broader computational principles.

The trimaximal mixing scheme (TM$_2$) yields a 	extit{``magic"} neutrino mass matrix ($M_
u$) capable of fitting neutrino oscillation data. In this study, we introduce a phenomenological ansatz for $M_
u$ by expanding upon this magic symmetry to minimize free parameters, thus enhancing the model's predictive power. Within the TM$_2$ framework, the neutrino mixing parameters, effective Majorana mass $m_{ee}$, and $CP$ invariants ($J_{CP}, I_1, I_2$) display significant correlations. A key characteristic of this model is the necessity of a non-maximal $	heta_{23}$ angle to allow for $CP$ violation detectable in oscillation experiments. The observables $m_{ee}$ and the sum of neutrino masses ($\sum m_i$) provide crucial insights into the unknown neutrino mass hierarchy. The lower limit on $m_{ee}$ predicted by the model under TM$_2$ with inverted hierarchy falls within the detection range of $0
u eta eta$ decay experiments. However, the cosmological upper bound of $0.12$ eV on $\sum m_i$ (at 95\% confidence level) excludes the inverted hierarchy, leaving TM$_2$ with normal hierarchy as the sole viable option. Furthermore, we demonstrate a scenario where such a neutrino mass matrix construction can be achieved using $\Delta(54)$ symmetry within a Type-I+II seesaw mechanism.

We examine a domain from which a small, compact set with zero Lebesgue measure has been excised. Our primary focus is the spectrum of the Neumann Laplacian defined on this modified domain. We demonstrate that the Laplacian's spectrum converges, in terms of Hausdorff distance, to the spectrum of the Laplacian on the original, unperturbed domain.

The identification of superconducting nickelates has renewed optimism for understanding the mechanism behind high-$T_{\textrm{c}}$ superconductivity in the structurally similar cuprates. Unlike cuprates, where the superconducting gap forms on a single band of a quasi-2D Fermi surface, nickelates exhibit a multi-band electronic structure with three-dimensional characteristics. This discrepancy prompts a critical inquiry into the necessity of a 2D nature for high-$T_{\textrm{c}}$ superconductivity. By utilizing a combination of dynamical mean field theory and the GW method, we discovered that a Kondo effect, driven by strong correlations between Nd-4$f$ and Ni-3$d$ electrons, emerges at low temperatures. This Kondo effect alters the Fermi surface topology, resulting in a 3D multi-band structure. Notably, this effect is readily disrupted by lattice modulation, which restores a quasi-2D nature. These insights provide a clear explanation for the discrepancies in superconductivity occurrence and electrical resistivity behavior observed between bulk NdNiO$_{2}$ and its films.

We provide a comprehensive calculation of the expected rate for the Geomagnetic Conversion of Solar Axions to X-rays (GECOSAX) along the trajectory of an x-ray satellite, incorporating realistic orbital paths and temporal propagation. Our analysis employs a realistic model of the Earth's magnetic field that accurately reflects its spatial non-uniformity and includes the impact of the Earth's atmosphere on x-ray propagation when determining axion-photon conversion probabilities. Using actual background measurements from the SUZAKU satellite to estimate potential sensitivities for the axion-photon coupling $g_{a\gamma}$, we demonstrate that, with a detector area of $10^3 \text{ cm}^2$ and approximately $10^6 \text{ s}$ of data, GECOSAX can achieve a $2\sigma$ limit of $g_{a\gamma} < (4.7\text{--}6.6) \times 10^{-11} \text{ GeV}^{-1}$ for axion masses $m_a < 10^{-4} \text{ eV}$. This sensitivity significantly surpasses current laboratory constraints on $g_{a\gamma}$.

We develop specific integral frameworks for the cores of reduced tame extended affine Lie algebras with a rank of 2 or higher. A primary instrument in this construction involves extending the concept of Chevalley automorphisms to the realm of extended affine Lie algebras. Consequently, we define groups of extended affine Lie type corresponding to the adjoint representation over any given field.

Recent advancements in natural language understanding have been driven by large pre-trained Transformer networks. Nevertheless, their substantial size creates significant hurdles for fine-tuning and online deployment, primarily due to latency and cost limitations. Emerging hardware that supports both N:M semi-structured sparsity and low-precision integer computation offers a promising avenue to enhance the efficiency of deep neural network serving. Despite this potential, systematic research on how much pre-trained Transformers benefit from combining these techniques, as well as optimal compression strategies for each component, remains scarce.
